title.zh: 卷149 志一百二十四 交通一 铁路
title.raw: 卷149 志一百二十四 交通一 铁路

sentences.zh: 有清之世，歐洲諸國以製器相競致強富，路船郵電，因利乘權。

translations.literal: In the Qing era, the nations of Europe vied in manufacturing to achieve strength and wealth, and through railways, ships, post, and telegraph they seized advantage by exploiting opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qing dynasty, European powers competed in industrial manufacture to grow strong and rich, then used railways, steam navigation, postal service, and telegraphy to press their advantage whenever opportunity arose.

sentences.zh: 道光朝五口通商，各國踵跡至。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang reign the five treaty ports were opened to trade, and the various nations followed one after another in coming.
translations.idiomatic: After the five treaty ports opened under the Daoguang emperor, foreign powers arrived in succession.

sentences.zh: 中外棣通，外舟侵入我江海置郵通商地。

translations.literal: China and abroad were linked in concord; foreign vessels entered our rivers and seas and established postal and commercial treaty sites.
translations.idiomatic: As contacts between China and the outside world grew, foreign ships entered Chinese rivers and seas and set up treaty-port posts and trading stations.

sentences.zh: 大北、大東兩公司海底電線貫太平洋、大西洋而來，亦駢集我海上，駸駸有返客為主之勢焉。

translations.literal: The submarine cables of the Great Northern and Great Eastern companies ran through the Pacific and Atlantic oceans to arrive here, and they also gathered thickly off our coasts, gradually taking on the aspect of guests returning to become masters.
translations.idiomatic: Submarine telegraph cables laid by the Great Northern and Great Eastern companies spanned the Pacific and Atlantic to reach China, clustering along the coast until foreign operators seemed on the verge of turning from guests into masters.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章、郭嵩燾諸臣以國權、商務、戎機所關甚鉅，抗疏論列。

translations.literal: Ministers such as Li Hongzhang and Guo Songtao, because national sovereignty, commerce, and military affairs were implicated to a very great degree, submitted memorials resisting and setting forth arguments in array.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang, Guo Songtao, and other officials repeatedly memorialized the throne, arguing that sovereignty, trade, and military readiness were at stake on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 其始也阻於眾咻，其繼也卒排群議而次第建設之，開我國數千年未有之奇局。

translations.literal: At first they were blocked by the clamor of the multitude; afterward they finally overcame collective debate and built these projects in sequence, opening a marvelous situation our country had not seen in several thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: At first public uproar blocked them, but they eventually pushed past collective opposition and built the new systems step by step, inaugurating a transformation China had not seen in millennia.

sentences.zh: 於時鴻章總督直隸，領北洋通商大臣，忍詬負重，卒觀厥成。

translations.literal: At that time Hongzhang was governor-general of Zhili and held the post of Northern Sea trade superintendent; he endured abuse and bore heavy burdens, and in the end witnessed its completion.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang was then governor-general of Zhili and superintendent of trade for the Northern Seas; though he bore ridicule and heavy responsibility, he lived to see the enterprise through.

sentences.zh: 長江招商輪船局始於。

translations.literal: The Yangtze China Merchants Steam Navigation Bureau had its beginning at.
translations.idiomatic: The China Merchants Steam Navigation Company on the Yangtze was established at that time.

sentences.zh: 逮光緒三年，有唐山胥各庄鐵路之築。

translations.literal: By the third year of the Guangxu reign there was the building of the railway from Tangshan to Xugezhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3 (1877) work began on the Tangshan–Xugezhuang railway.

sentences.zh: 四年，設郵政局。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Postal Bureau was established.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the postal administration was founded.

sentences.zh: 五年，設電線於大沽、北塘海口砲台，西達天津。

translations.literal: In the fifth year telegraph lines were set up at the Dagu and Beitang coastal batteries, extending west to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 5 telegraph wires linked the coastal forts at Dagu and Beitang westward to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，歲展月拓，分途並進。

translations.literal: From that time onward, year by year they expanded month by month, advancing by separate routes in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the network spread month by month and year by year, with projects advancing on many fronts at once.

sentences.zh: 輪船則有官輪、商輪之別，鐵路則有官辦、商辦之別，電線則有部辦、省辦之別，郵政則有總局、分局之別。

translations.literal: For steamships there was the distinction between official and merchant fleets; for railways between government-run and merchant-run lines; for telegraph wires between ministry-run and province-run lines; for postal service between general bureau and branch bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Steam navigation split into official and merchant fleets; railways into government and private lines; telegraphy into central and provincial systems; and the post into head offices and branches.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，郵傳部計路之通車者逾萬里，線之通電者九萬餘里，局之通郵者四千餘處。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign the Ministry of Posts and Communications calculated routes open to traffic at more than ten thousand li, lines open to telegraphy at more than ninety thousand li, and bureaus open to mail at more than four thousand places.
translations.idiomatic: By the early Xuantong period the Ministry of Communications reported more than ten thousand li of railway in service, more than ninety thousand li of telegraph wire, and more than four thousand post offices.

sentences.zh: 歲之所入，路約銀二千萬，電約一千萬，郵六百餘萬，而歲支外所盈無幾，無乃分其利者眾歟？

translations.literal: Annual receipts were roughly twenty million taels of silver for railways, about ten million for telegraphy, and more than six million for post; yet yearly expenditures left little surplus—was it not because those sharing the profits were many?
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue ran to some twenty million taels from railways, ten million from telegraphy, and six million from the post, yet expenses left little margin—perhaps because too many parties were dividing the profits.

sentences.zh: 昔者車行日不過百里，舟則視風勢水流為遲疾，廷寄軍書，驛人介馬俟，盡日夕行不過六七百里已耳。

translations.literal: Formerly carts traveled no more than a hundred li a day, and boats depended on wind and current for speed or slowness; court dispatches and military documents sent by courier and relay horse, even traveling day and night, went no more than six or seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times carts covered scarcely a hundred li a day, and boats moved only as wind and current allowed; even urgent court and military dispatches by relay horse rarely exceeded six or seven hundred li in a full day and night.

sentences.zh: 今則京漢之車，津滬之舟，計程各二三千里而遙，不出三日，郵之附舟車以達者如之。

translations.literal: Now the Beijing–Hankou train and the Tianjin–Shanghai steamer, each route two or three thousand li distant, reach their ends in no more than three days; mail sent attached to boat or cart arrives likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Beijing–Hankou railway and Tianjin–Shanghai steamers, each spanning two or three thousand li, complete the journey in under three days, and mail carried on ship or train keeps the same pace.

sentences.zh: 若以電線達者，數萬里外瞬息立至。

translations.literal: If sent by telegraph wire, tens of thousands of li away it arrives in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: By telegraph a message tens of thousands of li distant arrives in an instant.

sentences.zh: 民情慮始難，觀成易，故船、電、路皆有商辦名。

translations.literal: Popular sentiment fears beginnings but accepts accomplished facts easily; therefore ships, telegraph, and railways all bore the name of merchant operation.
translations.idiomatic: The people dread novelty but readily accept what is already built, so steam navigation, telegraphy, and railways were all launched under merchant-management labels.

sentences.zh: 顧言利之臣胥欲籠為國有，以加諸電商者加之川漢自辦之路，操之過激，商股抗議者輒罪之。

translations.literal: Yet officials who spoke of profit all wished to seize them as state property; what they imposed on telegraph merchants they also imposed on the Sichuan–Hankou self-built railway, handling matters too harshly, and merchant shareholders who protested were then punished as criminals.
translations.idiomatic: Yet profit-minded officials sought to bring everything under state control; the pressure applied to telegraph companies was turned on the merchant-built Sichuan–Hankou railway as well, and shareholders who objected were prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 淫刑而逞，以犯眾怒，黨人乘之，國本遂搖。

translations.literal: They indulged cruel punishments and acted willfully, provoking popular wrath; the revolutionaries seized the moment, and the foundation of the state was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive punishment and high-handedness enraged the public; revolutionaries exploited the unrest, and the dynasty’s foundations trembled.

sentences.zh: 孔子論治，以書同文、車同軌、行同倫為極盛。

translations.literal: Confucius in discussing governance took identical script, identical cart tracks, and identical moral norms as the height of flourishing order.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius described ideal governance as unified writing, uniform cart tracks, and shared moral standards.

sentences.zh: 清之天下，可謂同文同軌矣，惟行殊焉，而理亂頓異。

translations.literal: The realm under the Qing may be said to have shared script and shared tracks, yet conduct differed, and order and disorder suddenly diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qing, script and railways were unified nationwide, yet customs diverged—and with them the difference between order and chaos.

sentences.zh: 則知伏羲氏所謂通天下之志者，有形下之器，尤貴有形上之道以維繫之，未可重器而遺道也。

translations.literal: Then one knows that what Fuxi called communicating the will of all under Heaven—besides instruments in the realm of form, the Way in the realm of formlessness is especially precious for binding them together; one cannot value instruments and abandon the Way.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that Fuxi’s aim of harmonizing the will of the empire requires not only material technology but the moral order that sustains it; tools alone, without principle, will not suffice.

sentences.zh: 撰〈

translations.literal: Composed “
translations.idiomatic: The compilers prepared the “

sentences.zh: 交通志〉

translations.literal: Treatise on Communications”
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Communications”

sentences.zh: 鐵路創始於英吉利，各國踵而行之。

translations.literal: Railways originated in England, and the various nations followed in implementing them.
translations.idiomatic: Railways began in England, and other countries soon followed.

sentences.zh: 同治季年，海防議起，直督李鴻章數為執政者陳鐵路之利，不果行。

translations.literal: In the late Tongzhi reign coastal defense debates arose; Governor-General Li Hongzhang of Zhili repeatedly explained the benefits of railways to those in power, but the project was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During the late Tongzhi period, as coastal defense was debated, Li Hongzhang, governor-general of Zhili, repeatedly urged the court to build railways, but without success.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，英人擅築上海鐵路達吳淞，命鴻章禁止，因偕江督沈葆楨，檄盛宣懷等與英人議，卒以銀二十八萬兩購回，廢置不用，識者惜之。

translations.literal: In the early Guangxu reign the English unilaterally built a railway from Shanghai to Wusong; the court ordered Hongzhang to forbid it, and together with Governor-General Shen Baozhen of Jiangsu he issued a proclamation for Sheng Xuanhuai and others to negotiate with the English; in the end they purchased it back for 280,000 taels of silver, dismantled it, and left it unused—men of insight regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, British interests built a line from Shanghai to Wusong; the court directed Hongzhang to stop it, and with Jiangsu governor-general Shen Baozhen he had Sheng Xuanhuai negotiate a buyout for 280,000 taels, after which the track was dismantled and abandoned—a decision later lamented by informed observers.

sentences.zh: 三年，有商人築唐山至胥各庄鐵路八犬里，是為中國自築鐵路之始。

translations.literal: In the third year a merchant built a railway from Tangshan to Xugezhuang, eight miles in length—this was the beginning of railways built by China itself.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3 merchants completed an eight-mile railway from Tangshan to Xugezhuang—the first line built by Chinese initiative.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉銘傳入覲，疏言：「自古敵國外患，未有如今日之多且強也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liu Mingchuan came to audience and memorialized: “Since antiquity there have never been so many and so powerful foreign troubles as today.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 Liu Mingchuan presented himself at court and memorialized: “Never in history have foreign threats been so numerous and formidable as today.

sentences.zh: 一國有事，各國環窺，而俄地橫亙東、西、北，與我壤界交錯，尤為心腹之憂。

translations.literal: When one state has affairs, the various states look on from all sides; yet Russia’s territory stretches across east, west, and north, interlocking with our borders—it is an anxiety at the very heart.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble arises in one country, others watch from every side; Russia in particular spans east, west, and north and shares a long border with us, making it the gravest concern.

sentences.zh: 俄自歐洲起造鐵路，漸近浩罕，又將由海參崴開路以達琿春，此時之持滿不發者，以鐵路未成故也。

translations.literal: Russia has built railways from Europe, drawing gradually near Kokand, and will also open a route from Vladivostok to reach Hunchun; its restraint in not striking now is because the railway is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Russia is extending railways from Europe toward Kokand and plans another from Vladivostok to Hunchun; it holds back only because the lines are unfinished.

sentences.zh: 不出十年，禍且不測。

translations.literal: Within ten years disaster may come unpredictably.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years catastrophe may strike without warning.

sentences.zh: 日本一彈丸國耳，師西人之長技，恃有鐵路，亦遇事與我為難。

translations.literal: Japan is but a pellet of a state, yet by mastering Western techniques and relying on railways it also contends with us at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Japan is a tiny archipelago, yet by adopting Western technology and railways it repeatedly challenges us.

sentences.zh: 舍此不圖，自強恐無及矣。

translations.literal: If we do not plan for this, I fear self-strengthening will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we act now, self-strengthening may arrive too late.

sentences.zh: 自強之道，練兵造器，固宜次第舉行。

translations.literal: The path of self-strengthening—training troops and manufacturing weapons—should indeed be undertaken in due order.
translations.idiomatic: Self-strengthening requires training armies and manufacturing arms, and these should proceed in turn.

sentences.zh: 然其機括，則在於急造鐵路。

translations.literal: Yet the pivot lies in urgently building railways.
translations.idiomatic: But the decisive lever is rapid railway construction.

sentences.zh: 鐵路之利，於漕務、賑務、商務、礦務、釐捐、行旅者，不可殫述，而於用兵尤不可緩。

translations.literal: The benefits of railways for grain transport, relief work, commerce, mining, transit duties, and travelers cannot be fully enumerated, and for military use they are especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Railways aid grain shipment, disaster relief, trade, mining, transit levies, and travel beyond counting, and are above all indispensable to the military.

sentences.zh: 中國幅員遼闊，北邊綿亙萬里，毗連俄界；

translations.literal: China’s territory is vast and broad; the northern frontier extends ten thousand li, adjoining Russian territory;
translations.idiomatic: China is immense: the northern frontier runs thousands of li along the Russian border;

sentences.zh: 通商各海口，又與各國共之。

translations.literal: the treaty ports open to trade are also shared with the various nations.
translations.idiomatic: every maritime treaty port is open to foreign powers as well.

sentences.zh: 畫疆而守，則防不勝防，馳逐往來，則鞭長莫及。

translations.literal: To guard fixed boundaries is to defend more positions than can be held; to rush back and forth is to find the whip too short to reach the horse.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed garrisons cannot guard every point, while rapid movement over such distances exceeds any commander’s reach.

sentences.zh: 惟鐵路一開，則東西南北呼吸相通，視敵所趨，相機策應，雖萬里之遙，數日可至，百萬之眾，一呼而集。

translations.literal: Only when railways are opened do east, west, south, and north breathe together in communication; watching where the enemy turns, one responds with measured plans—even ten thousand li away one arrives in days, and a million troops assemble at a single call.
translations.idiomatic: Once railways link the realm, troops and supplies move in every direction; commanders can shift forces to meet the enemy wherever he appears—distances of ten thousand li shrink to days, and armies of a million gather on command.

sentences.zh: 且兵合則強，分則弱。

translations.literal: Moreover, when troops unite they are strong; divided they are weak.
translations.idiomatic: Concentrated armies are strong; scattered ones are weak.

sentences.zh: 以中國十八省計之，兵非不多，餉非不足，然此疆彼界，各具一心，遇有兵端，自顧不暇，徵餉調兵，無力承應。

translations.literal: Counting China’s eighteen provinces, troops are not few nor funds insufficient, yet each region has its own mind; when war comes each looks to itself, and when levies and troop transfers are ordered none can answer the call.
translations.idiomatic: The eighteen provinces have ample soldiers and revenue, yet each province thinks for itself; in war none can spare strength for another, and central orders for funds or troops go unanswered.

sentences.zh: 若鐵路告成，則聲勢聯絡，血脈貫通，裁兵節餉，並成勁旅，防邊防海，轉運槍砲，朝發夕至，駐防之兵即可為游擊之旅，十八省合為一氣，一兵可抵十數兵之用。

translations.literal: If railways are completed, then prestige links up and the vital channels connect; armies may be cut and pay saved while forming crack forces; coastal and frontier defense, transport of guns and cannon, depart at dawn and arrive at dusk; garrison troops can become mobile columns; the eighteen provinces unite in one breath, and one soldier can do the work of ten or more.
translations.idiomatic: With railways complete, the empire’s sinews knit together: forces can be trimmed yet made more effective, guns rushed to coast or border overnight, garrisons turned into mobile columns, and the eighteen provinces act as one—so that one soldier counts for ten.

sentences.zh: 將來兵權餉權，俱在朝廷，內重外輕，不為疆臣所牽制矣。

translations.literal: In future military authority and revenue authority will both rest in the court; inner weight and outer lightness, and regional ministers will no longer hold the state in check.
translations.idiomatic: Military and fiscal power would return to the center, strengthening Beijing against the provinces and freeing the throne from dependence on regional strongmen.

sentences.zh: 方今國計絀於邊防，民生困於釐卡。

translations.literal: At present state finances are strained at the frontier, and the people’s livelihood is trapped by transit stations and tax barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Today the treasury is drained by frontier defense while common people suffer under likin barriers.

sentences.zh: 各國通商，爭奪利權，財賦日竭，後患方殷。

translations.literal: The various nations trade and contend for profit rights; state wealth daily fails and later troubles grow severe.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign trade competition drains revenue, and the danger ahead grows worse.

sentences.zh: 如有鐵路，收費足以養兵，則釐卡可以酌裁，裕國便民，無逾於此。

translations.literal: If there are railways, toll receipts suffice to maintain troops, then transit stations may be reduced as appropriate—enriching the state and benefiting the people, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Railway tolls could support the army and allow likin to be cut—enriching the state and easing burdens on the people.

sentences.zh: 今欲乘時立辦，莫如籌借洋債。

translations.literal: To seize the moment and establish this at once, nothing is better than raising foreign loans.
translations.idiomatic: The swiftest course is to borrow foreign capital now.

sentences.zh: 中國要路有二：南路一由清江經山東，一由漢口經河南，俱達京師；

translations.literal: China’s essential routes are two: the southern route—one from Qingjiang through Shandong, one from Hankou through Henan—both reaching the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Two trunk lines matter most: southward, one from Qingjiang via Shandong and one from Hankou via Henan, both to Beijing;

sentences.zh: 北路由京師東通盛京，西達甘肅。

translations.literal: the northern route from Beijing east to Mukden and west to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: northward, from Beijing east to Mukden and west to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 若未能同時並舉，可先修清江至京一路，與本年擬修之電線相為表裡。

translations.literal: If they cannot be built all at once, the Qingjiang–Beijing line may be built first, complementing the telegraph line planned for this year.
translations.idiomatic: If both cannot be built together, begin with Qingjiang to Beijing, paired with the telegraph line already planned.

sentences.zh: 事下直督李鴻章、江督劉坤一議覆。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to Governor-General Li Hongzhang of Zhili and Governor-General Liu Kunyi of Jiangsu for deliberation and reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to Li Hongzhang in Zhili and Liu Kunyi in Jiangsu for joint review.

sentences.zh: 鴻章言：「鐵路之設，關於國計、軍政、京畿、民生、轉運、郵政、礦務、招商、輪船、行旅者，其利甚溥。

translations.literal: Hongzhang said: “The establishment of railways concerns state finances, military administration, the capital region, people’s livelihood, transport, postal service, mining, attracting merchants, steam navigation, and travelers—the benefits are very broad.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang replied that railways touched state finance, military affairs, the capital, livelihood, transport, post, mining, commerce, shipping, and travel, with vast benefits.

sentences.zh: 而借用洋債，外人於鐵路把持侵佔，與妨害國用諸端，亦不可不防。

translations.literal: Yet in borrowing foreign debt, foreigners’ control and encroachment over railways and the various ways they harm national utility must also be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: Yet foreign loans risk foreign control of railways and other injuries to national interest, which must be guarded against.

sentences.zh: 」坤一以妨兒民生、釐稅為言。

translations.literal: ” Kunyi spoke on the grounds of hindering people’s livelihood and transit taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyi argued that railways would harm livelihoods and likin revenue.

sentences.zh: 學士張家驤言興修鐵路有三大弊。

translations.literal: Academician Zhang Jiaxiang said building railways had three great harms.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Zhang Jiaxiang listed three major evils in railway construction.

sentences.zh: 復下其疏於鴻章，鴻章力主銘傳言。

translations.literal: His memorial was again sent down to Hongzhang, and Hongzhang strongly upheld Mingchuan’s words.
translations.idiomatic: The court forwarded Zhang’s memorial to Hongzhang, who again defended Mingchuan’s position.

sentences.zh: 會台官合疏力爭，侍講張楷言九不利，御史洪良品言五害，語尤激切。

translations.literal: Taiwan officials jointly memorialized in force, Expositor Zhang Kai listed nine disadvantages, and Censor Hong Liangpin listed five harms—their language especially vehement.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan officials memorialized en masse; expositor Zhang Kai cited nine drawbacks and censor Hong Liangpin five harms, all in fierce terms.

sentences.zh: 以廷臣諫止者多，詔罷其議。

translations.literal: Because many at court remonstrated to stop it, an edict halted the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: So many officials opposed the plan that the throne ordered the project dropped.

sentences.zh: 嗣是無復有言之者矣。

translations.literal: After this no one spoke of it again.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the subject was not raised again for years.

sentences.zh: 十一年，既與法國議和，朝廷念海防不可弛，詔各臣工切籌善後。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, after peace was made with France, the court mindful that coastal defense could not relax ordered all officials to deliberate earnestly on follow-up measures.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 11, after peace with France, the court ordered officials to plan seriously for coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章言：「法事起後，借洋債累二千萬，十年分起籌還，更無力籌水師之歲需。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang said: “After the French affair began, foreign loans accumulated to twenty million taels, to be repaid in installments over ten years; there is no further strength to fund the navy’s annual needs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang wrote that war with France had forced twenty million taels in foreign debt, repayable over ten years, leaving no margin for the navy’s yearly budget.

sentences.zh: 開源之道，當效西法採煤鐵、造鐵路、興商政。

translations.literal: The way to open new revenue is to follow Western methods in mining coal and iron, building railways, and promoting commercial administration.
translations.idiomatic: New revenue must come from Western-style coal and iron mining, railways, and commercial reform.

sentences.zh: 礦藏固為美富，鐵路實有遠利。

translations.literal: Mineral deposits are indeed rich and beautiful, but railways truly have long-term profit.
translations.idiomatic: Minerals are abundant, but railways promise the greater long-term gain.

sentences.zh: 但招商集股，難遽踴躍，官又無可資助。

translations.literal: Yet attracting merchant investment is hard to accomplish quickly, and the government has nothing with which to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant investment was slow to materialize, and the state could offer little support.

sentences.zh: 若輕息假洋款為之，雖各國所恆有，乃群情所駭詫，非聖明主持於上，誰敢破眾議以冒不韙？

translations.literal: If one lightly borrows foreign funds at low interest to do this—though all nations commonly do so—it is what popular feeling finds shocking; unless the sage ruler leads from above, who dares break collective opinion and court disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: Low-interest foreign loans, common abroad, would shock public opinion at home; without firm imperial backing, who would brave the outcry?

sentences.zh: 」大學士左宗棠條上七事，一言宜仿造鐵路：「外國以經商為本，因商造路，因路治兵，轉運靈通，無往不利。

translations.literal: ” Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang submitted seven items in a memorial, one saying railways should be imitated: “Foreign countries take commerce as their foundation; because of commerce they build roads, because of roads they organize troops—transport is nimble and nothing is unprofitable.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang submitted seven proposals, including railways: “Western nations rest on commerce; commerce builds railways, railways organize armies—flexible transport makes everything profitable.

sentences.zh: 其未建以前，阻撓固甚，一經告成，民因而富，國因而強，人物因而倍盛，有利無害，固有明徵。

translations.literal: Before they were built, obstruction was indeed severe; once completed, the people grew rich thereby, the state grew strong thereby, and men and affairs flourished doubly—benefit without harm has clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: Opposition was fierce before construction, yet once lines opened, wealth and power followed—proof that railways help without harm.

sentences.zh: 電報、輪船，中國所無，一旦有之，則為不可少之物。

translations.literal: Telegraph and steamships were things China did not have; once it had them they became indispensable.
translations.idiomatic: Telegraph and steamships were unknown in China until introduced; then they became indispensable.

sentences.zh: 倘鐵路造成，其利尤溥。

translations.literal: If railways are completed, the profit is especially vast.
translations.idiomatic: Railways would bring even greater benefit.

sentences.zh: 清江至通州宜先設立鐵路，以通南北之樞，一便於轉漕，而商務必有起色；

translations.literal: From Qingjiang to Tongzhou a railway should first be established to link the pivot of north and south—on one hand convenient for grain transport, and commerce will surely revive;
translations.idiomatic: He urged a line from Qingjiang to Tongzhou to join north and south—speeding grain transport and reviving trade;

sentences.zh: 一便於徵調，而額兵即可多裁。

translations.literal: on one hand convenient for levy and transfer, and the regular army may then be greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: and speeding troop movement so standing armies could be cut.

sentences.zh: 且為費僅數百萬，由官招商股試辦，即可舉行，且與地方民生並無妨礙。

translations.literal: The cost is only several million; the government may invite merchant shares on a trial basis and it can be carried out, and it does not obstruct local people’s livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Costing only a few million taels, it could be tried with merchant shares without harming local livelihood.

sentences.zh: 迨辦有成效，再添設分支。

translations.literal: When it is done with results, branch lines may be added.
translations.idiomatic: Branches could follow once the main line proved successful.

sentences.zh: 至推廣西北一路，尤為日後必然之勢。

translations.literal: As for extending the northwest route, that is especially a tendency of later days that must come.
translations.idiomatic: Extension northwestward would inevitably follow.

sentences.zh: 」疏下王大臣議，雖善其言而不能用也。

translations.literal: ” The memorial was sent down to princes and ministers for deliberation; though they approved his words they could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred the memorial to the grand council, which approved Zuo’s reasoning but took no action.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，鴻章復言：「陶城、臨清間二百餘里，運道淤墊，請試辦鐵道，為南北大道樞紐。

translations.literal: That winter Hongzhang again said: “Between Taocheng and Linqing, more than two hundred li, the transport channel is silted and blocked; I request a trial railway as the hub of the north–south great road.
translations.idiomatic: Later that winter Hongzhang proposed a trial line between Taocheng and Linqing, where the Grand Canal was silted, as the main north–south artery.

sentences.zh: 」上用漕督崧駿等言，格不行。

translations.literal: ” The emperor followed the words of Grain Transport Superintendent Song Jun and others and rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Grain Transport Superintendent Song Jun and others and refused.

sentences.zh: 初，法、越事起，以運輸不便，軍事幾敗。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the French–Vietnamese affair arose, because transport was inconvenient military affairs nearly failed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French war over Vietnam began, poor transport nearly cost the campaign.

sentences.zh: 事平，執政者始知鐵路關係軍事至要。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, those in power first understood that railways were vitally related to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After peace, leaders finally grasped how critical railways were to war.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，海軍衙門王大臣奕枻等言：「鐵路之議，歷有年所，毀譽紛紜，莫衷一是。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year the Naval Affairs Yamen princes and ministers Yi Kuang and others said: “The discussion of railways has gone on for years; praise and blame have been mixed, and no single view has prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13 spring, Prince Yi Kuang and colleagues at the Naval Affairs Yamen reported that debate over railways had raged for years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 自經前歲戰事，始悉局外空談與局中實際，判然兩途。

translations.literal: Only after last year’s fighting did one know that idle talk outside the affair and the actual situation within it are two entirely different paths.
translations.idiomatic: Combat had shown how empty outside opinion was compared with battlefield reality.

sentences.zh: 臣奕枻總理事務，見聞較切。

translations.literal: Your servant Yi Kuang oversees affairs and has comparatively close knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Kuang, overseeing affairs daily, had seen this firsthand.

sentences.zh: 臣曾紀澤出使八年，親見西洋各國輪車鐵路之益。

translations.literal: Your servant Zeng Jize served eight years abroad and personally witnessed the benefits of Western nations’ carriage railways.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Jize, after eight years as envoy abroad, had seen Western railways at work.

sentences.zh: 現公同酌覈，調兵運械，貴在便捷，自當擇要而圖。

translations.literal: Now jointly weighing and examining, transferring troops and shipping arms values swiftness above all; one should naturally select essentials and plan.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed that moving troops and arms required speed and that priority projects should be chosen.

sentences.zh: 據天津司道營員等稟，直隸海岸綿長，防守不易，轉運尤艱。

translations.literal: According to memorials from Tianjin circuit intendants and staff, the Zhili coast is long and defense difficult, and transport especially arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin officials reported that Zhili’s long coastline was hard to defend and supply.

sentences.zh: 請將開平至閻庄商辦鐵路，南接大沽北岸八十餘里，先行接造，再由大沽至天津百餘里，逐漸興修。

translations.literal: They request extending the merchant-built railway from Kaiping to Yanzhuang south to connect with the north bank of Dagu, more than eighty li, to be built first; then from Dagu to Tianjin, more than a hundred li, to be gradually constructed.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed linking the merchant Kaiping–Yanzhuang line south eighty-odd li to the north shore of Dagu, then building gradually from Dagu to Tianjin, another hundred-odd li.

sentences.zh: 津沽鐵路告成，續辦開平迤北至山海關，則提督周盛波所部萬人，馳騁援應，不啻數萬人之用。

translations.literal: When the Tianjin–Dagu railway is completed, continuing north from Kaiping to Shanhaiguan would let Brigadier Zhou Shengbo’s ten thousand men ride to aid as if they were tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Completing Tianjin–Dagu and extending Kaiping north to Shanhaiguan would let General Zhou Shengbo’s ten thousand men respond with the effect of many times that number.

sentences.zh: 此項海防要工，集資不易，應以官款興辦，調兵勇協同工作，以期速成。

translations.literal: This coastal defense work is hard to fund; government funds should build it, with soldiers laboring together, to finish quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Because coastal defense funds were scarce, official money and soldier labor should finish the line quickly.

sentences.zh: 如蒙俞允，即派員督率開平公司經理。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty approves, officials will be dispatched to supervise the Kaiping company’s management.
translations.idiomatic: Upon approval, officials would supervise the Kaiping company’s work.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 明年，路成。

translations.literal: The next year the line was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the railway opened.

sentences.zh: 總理衙門奏言：「新造津沽鐵路，自天津府城經塘沽、蘆台以至閻庄，長一百七十五里，其自閻庄至灤州之唐山，長八十里，為各商舊造鐵路。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen memorialized: “The newly built Tianjin–Dagu railway runs from Tianjin prefectural city through Tanggu and Lutai to Yanzhuang, 175 li in length; from Yanzhuang to Tangshan in Luanzhou, 80 li, is the merchants’ old railway.
translations.idiomatic: The Zongli Yamen reported that the new Tianjin–Dagu line ran 175 li from Tianjin through Tanggu and Lutai to Yanzhuang, joining the merchants’ existing 80-li Yanzhuang–Tangshan section.

sentences.zh: 新舊鐵路首尾銜接，輪車通行快利，為輪船所不及。

translations.literal: Old and new railways join head to tail; carriage travel is swift and advantageous, beyond what steamships can match.
translations.idiomatic: Linked end to end, trains ran faster than steamers could match.

sentences.zh: 通塞之權，操之自我，斷無利器假人之慮。

translations.literal: The power to open or block rests in ourselves; there is absolutely no worry of lending a sharp weapon to others.
translations.idiomatic: Control of traffic remained in Chinese hands, with no fear of giving a strategic weapon to foreigners.

sentences.zh: 由此經營推廣，一遇徵兵運械，輓粟飛芻，咄嗟可致；

translations.literal: By this management and extension, whenever troops are levied and arms transported, hauling grain and flying fodder can be achieved in an instant;
translations.idiomatic: Extended in this way, the network could move troops and supplies at a word—grain and fodder arriving as if by magic;

sentences.zh: 商民貿遷，無遠弗屆，榛莽之地，可變通衢，洵為今日自強之急務。

translations.literal: Merchants and people in trade migration reach everywhere without distance; wilderness places can become thoroughfares—it is truly today’s urgent task for self-strengthening.
translations.idiomatic: commerce would reach every corner, wasteland become highways, and self-strengthening gain its most urgent instrument.

sentences.zh: 會粵商陳承德請接造天津至通州鐵路，略言：「現造鐵路，其所入不敷養路之用。

translations.literal: At the same time Guangdong merchant Chen Chengde requested to continue building the railway from Tianjin to Tongzhou, briefly saying: “The railways now being built—their receipts do not suffice for maintaining the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guangdong merchant Chen Chengde petitioned to extend the line from Tianjin to Tongzhou, noting that existing railways barely covered maintenance costs.

sentences.zh: 如接造此路，既可抽還造路借本，並可報效海軍經費。

translations.literal: If this route is continued, one may both withdraw and repay borrowed capital for building the road and also offer surplus to naval funds.
translations.idiomatic: Extending it, he argued, could repay construction loans and contribute to the navy.

sentences.zh: 」直督李鴻章以聞，已如所請矣；

translations.literal: ” Governor-General Li Hongzhang reported this, and it was already approved as requested;
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang reported the request and the court had approved it;

sentences.zh: 於時舉朝駭然，尚書翁同龢、奎潤，閣學文治，學士徐會灃，御史余聯沅、洪良品、屠仁守交章諫阻。

translations.literal: at that time the whole court was alarmed; Minister Weng Tonghe, Kui Run, Hanlin Academician Wen Zhi, Academician Xu Huiyi, and Censors Yu Lianyuan, Hong Liangpin, and Tu Renshou submitted memorials in succession to remonstrate and block it.
translations.idiomatic: then the court erupted: Ministers Weng Tonghe and Kui Run, Hanlin academician Wen Zhi, academician Xu Huiyi, and censors Yu Lianyuan, Hong Liangpin, and Tu Renshou memorialized fiercely against it.

sentences.zh: 其大端不外資敵、擾民、失業三者，亦有言宜於邊地及設於德州、濟寧以通河運者。

translations.literal: Their main points were nothing beyond aiding the enemy, disturbing the people, and loss of livelihood; some also said it was suitable in frontier regions or should be set at Dezhou and Jining to connect with canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: Critics chiefly cited three evils—arming the enemy, harming the people, and destroying jobs—while others urged building only on the frontier or at Dezhou and Jining to serve the canal.

sentences.zh: 命俱下海軍衙門。

translations.literal: The court ordered all memorials sent to the Naval Affairs Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: All memorials were referred to the Naval Affairs Yamen.

sentences.zh: 尋議上，略言：「原奏所慮各節，一在資敵。

translations.literal: Soon they deliberated and submitted upward, briefly saying: “The concerns in the original memorials—first, aiding the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen replied that critics feared three things, beginning with aiding the enemy.

sentences.zh: 不知敵至而車已收回，豈有資敵之慮？

translations.literal: They do not know that when the enemy arrives the trains are already withdrawn—how can there be worry of aiding the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: But if trains were withdrawn when enemies approached, that fear vanished.

sentences.zh: 一在擾民。

translations.literal: Second, disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Second, disturbing the people.

sentences.zh: 建設鐵路，首在繞避民間廬舍丘墓，其萬難繞避者，亦給重價，諭令遷徙，可無擾民之事。

translations.literal: In building railways, the first priority is to bypass popular houses and tombs; where bypass is utterly impossible, heavy price is also paid and people are instructed to relocate—there need be no matter of disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Routes would avoid homes and graves wherever possible and compensate relocations generously.

sentences.zh: 一在失業。

translations.literal: Third, loss of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Third, loss of livelihood.

sentences.zh: 鐵路興而商業盛，謀生之途益廣，更鮮失業之虞。

translations.literal: When railways flourish, commerce flourishes; paths to make a living grow broader, and there is even less worry of lost livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Railways, they argued, would expand commerce and employment rather than destroy them.

sentences.zh: 津通之路，非為富國，亦非利商，外助海軍相輔之需，內備徵兵入衛之用。

translations.literal: The Tianjin–Tongzhou route is not for enriching the state nor for profiting merchants; outwardly it assists naval mutual support needs, inwardly it prepares for levying troops to enter and guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin–Tongzhou line served naval defense and troop movement, not merchant profit or state revenue alone.

sentences.zh: 乃議者不察底蘊，不相匡助，或竟道聽途說，或竟憑空結撰，連章論列，上瀆天聽。

translations.literal: Yet those who debated did not examine the underlying truth, did not assist one another, or even repeated hearsay, or even fabricated from nothing, linking memorials in series and polluting the imperial ear.
translations.idiomatic: Opponents, failing to grasp this, spread rumors and bombarded the throne with serial memorials.

sentences.zh: 方今環球諸國，各治甲兵，其往也，非干羽所能格，其來也，非牛餼所能退，全視中華之強弱，為相安相擾之樞機。

translations.literal: At present all nations under the globe each maintain armed forces; in going forth, civil rites and music cannot restrain them; in coming, cattle and grain cannot repel them—all depends on whether China is strong or weak, as the pivot of mutual peace or mutual disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Nations arm themselves; ritual and tribute no longer deter them—only China’s strength decides whether they stay peaceful or press their advantage.

sentences.zh: 臣等創修鐵路本意，不在效外洋之到處皆設，而專主利於用兵。

translations.literal: Your servants’ original intent in first building railways is not to imitate foreign countries’ setting them up everywhere, but solely to take advantage for military use.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen sought railways for military necessity, not to copy foreign models everywhere.

sentences.zh: 不僅修津通之路，而志期應援全局。

translations.literal: Not only building the Tianjin–Tongzhou route, but aiming in ambition to respond and aid the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin–Tongzhou line was meant to serve the whole strategic picture.

sentences.zh: 誠能於江南、趙北、關東、隴西各設重兵，各安鐵路，則軍行萬里無胼胝之勞，糧運千倉有瞬息之效，零星隊伍可撤可並，浮濫餉乾或裁或節。

translations.literal: If truly in Jiangnan, north of Zhao, east of the Pass, and west of Long one could station heavy troops and install railways in each place, then armies could march ten thousand li without the toil of blistered hands and feet, and grain transport from a thousand granaries would have the effect of an instant; scattered detachments could be withdrawn or combined, and redundant pay could be cut or saved.
translations.idiomatic: With railways in Jiangnan, Hebei, the northeast, and the northwest, armies could march ten thousand li without blistered feet, grain move from a thousand granaries in an instant, scattered units merge or disband, and wasteful pay be trimmed.

sentences.zh: 此外如海防河運，裨益實多，而通貨物、銷礦產、利行旅、便工役、速郵遞，利之所興，難以枚舉。

translations.literal: Besides this, such as coastal defense and canal transport, the practical benefits are indeed many; and circulating goods, selling mineral products, benefiting travelers, convenient labor and works, and swift postal dispatch—the benefits that arise are hard to enumerate one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal defense, canal transport, trade, mining, travel, labor, and post would all gain benefits beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 而事屬創辦，不厭求詳。

translations.literal: Yet because the matter is inaugural, one is not tired of seeking detail.
translations.idiomatic: Because the project was unprecedented, they welcomed thorough discussion.

sentences.zh: 請下沿江沿海各將軍督撫，各抒所見。

translations.literal: We request that along the rivers and coasts each general and governor-general state their views.
translations.idiomatic: They asked every coastal and riverine governor-general and general to submit opinions.

sentences.zh: 」遂如所請，命各詳議以聞。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon as requested, the court ordered each to deliberate in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed and ordered detailed reports.

sentences.zh: 台灣巡撫劉銘傳議由津沽造路至京師，護蘇撫黃彭年議先辦邊防、漕路，緩辦腹地及沿江沿海各省，而試行於津通。

translations.literal: Taiwan Governor Liu Mingchuan proposed building from Jingu to the capital; Acting Jiangsu Governor Huang Pengnian urged frontier and grain-route railways first, delaying the interior and coastal provinces while trial-building Tianjin–Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan governor Liu Mingchuan wanted a line from Tianjin to Beijing; acting Jiangsu governor Huang Pengnian favored frontier and canal routes first and only a trial at Tianjin–Tongzhou inland.

sentences.zh: 粵督張之洞請緩辦津通，改建腹省幹路，疏言：

translations.literal: Guangdong Governor Zhang Zhidong requested delaying Tianjin–Tongzhou and instead building interior trunk lines, memorializing:
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong governor Zhang Zhidong asked to postpone Tianjin–Tongzhou and build interior trunk lines instead, writing:

sentences.zh: 奏上，仍下海軍衙門。

translations.literal: The memorial went up and was again sent to the Naval Affairs Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial went again to the Naval Affairs Yamen.

sentences.zh: 尋復議上：「各國興辦鐵路，以幹路為經，以枝路為緯，有事則以路徵兵，無事則以商養路。

translations.literal: Soon they again deliberated and submitted: “The various nations in undertaking railways take trunk lines as warp and branch lines as weft; when there is business they levy troops by the road, when there is none merchants maintain the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen answered that nations used trunk lines as warp and branches as weft, moving troops in crisis and letting commerce maintain peacetime operations.

sentences.zh: 就五大洲言之，宜於西洋，宜於東洋，豈其獨不宜於中國？

translations.literal: Speaking of the five continents, it is suitable in the Western Ocean, suitable in the Eastern Ocean—how can it alone be unsuitable for China?
translations.idiomatic: If railways suited Europe and Japan, why not China?

sentences.zh: 就中國言之，或云宜於邊防，或云宜於腹地，豈其獨不宜於臣衙門所奏准之津通？

translations.literal: Speaking of China, some say it is suitable for frontier defense, some say for the interior—how can it alone be unsuitable for Tianjin–Tongzhou as your Yamen memorialized approval?
translations.idiomatic: If some said railways belonged on the frontier and others in the interior, why reject only the Yamen-approved Tianjin–Tongzhou line?

sentences.zh: 津通，畿東南一正幹也。

translations.literal: Tianjin–Tongzhou is one main trunk southeast of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin–Tongzhou was a main artery southeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 水路受沿海七省之委輸，陸路通關東三省之命脈。

translations.literal: By water it receives the delivery of seven coastal provinces; by land it connects the lifeblood of the three eastern provinces beyond the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Its waterways fed seven coastal provinces; its land route linked the three eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 豫鄂則畿西南一正幹也，控荊襄，達關隴，以一道扼七八省之沖。

translations.literal: Henan and Hubei are another main trunk southwest of the capital, controlling Jing and Xiang, reaching Tong and Long, with one route holding the choke point of seven or eight provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan–Hubei corridor was another trunk controlling the middle Yangtze and northwest passes.

sentences.zh: 初意徐議中原，而先以津沽便海防，繼以津通擴商利，區區二百里，其關係與豫鄂之千里略同。

translations.literal: The original intent was to discuss the central plain slowly while first using Jingu for coastal defense convenience, then using Tianjin–Tongzhou to expand commercial profit—a mere two hundred li, its importance roughly equal to a thousand li in Henan and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: They had meant to defer the central plain while using Tianjin first for coastal defense and Tianjin–Tongzhou for commerce—two hundred li as weighty as a thousand elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 今張之洞亦設為津通五宜審之說，其中所慮各節，前奏固已剖析無遺。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Zhidong also sets forth the theory of five points to examine for Tianjin–Tongzhou; among them the concerns in each section were already analyzed without remainder in the former memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong’s five objections to Tianjin–Tongzhou had already been answered in the earlier memorial.

sentences.zh: 惟事關創始，擇善而從。

translations.literal: Only because the matter concerns a beginning, one chooses the good and follows it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the enterprise was new, the court would choose the better course.

sentences.zh: 津通鐵路應即暫從緩辦，而盧漢必以漢口至信陽為首段，層遞而北，並改為盧溝、漢口兩路分投試辦，綜計需銀三千萬兩，以商股、官帑、洋債三者為集款之法。

translations.literal: The Tianjin–Tongzhou railway should for the present be temporarily deferred, while Lu-Han must take Hankou to Xinyang as the first section, layer by layer northward, and be changed to trial building by separate investment on the Lugou and Hankou routes, totaling a need of thirty million taels of silver, with merchant shares, official funds, and foreign debt as the three methods of raising funds.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin–Tongzhou would be deferred; the Lu-Han line would begin Hankou–Xinyang and proceed north in stages, with separate trial lines from Lugou and Hankou, costing thirty million taels from merchant stock, official funds, and foreign loans.

sentences.zh: 」議上，詔旨允之。

translations.literal: ” When the deliberation went up, an imperial edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 初，鴻章倡津通鐵路之議，舉朝以為不可，鴻章持之甚力。

translations.literal: Earlier Hongzhang had advocated the Tianjin–Tongzhou railway proposal; the whole court thought it impossible, yet Hongzhang held to it very firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang had long pushed Tianjin–Tongzhou against near-universal court opposition.

sentences.zh: 之洞特創盧漢幹路之說，調停其間，而醇親王奕枻復贊之於內，其事始定。

translations.literal: Zhidong specially created the theory of the Lu-Han trunk line, mediating between them, and Prince Chun Yi Kuang again endorsed it within, and the matter was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong’s Lu-Han trunk proposal, with Prince Chun Yi Kuang’s backing, finally settled the dispute.

sentences.zh: 然其時廷臣尚多不以盧漢造路為然，但無敢昌言者。

translations.literal: Yet at that time many at court still did not approve building the Lu-Han road, but none dared speak openly.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials still disliked Lu-Han but dared not say so openly.

sentences.zh: 故通政黃體芳謂鐵路不可借洋債以自累，而台臣亦有言黃河橋工難成者，以執政者堅持舉辦，久之浮議始息。

translations.literal: Therefore Remonstrance Bureau official Huang Tifang said railways could not borrow foreign debt to burden themselves, and Taiwan officials also said the Yellow River bridge work would be hard to complete; because those in power insisted on proceeding, after long time floating opinion finally ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huang Tifang warned against foreign debt; Taiwan memorialists doubted bridging the Yellow River; only firm leadership quieted the uproar.

sentences.zh: 鴻章與之洞書，謂局外議論紛歧，宜速開辦，免生枝節，之洞深然之。

translations.literal: Hongzhang wrote to Zhidong, saying outside opinion was mixed and construction should open quickly to avoid branching complications; Zhidong deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang urged Zhidong to build quickly before controversy grew; Zhidong agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，之洞總督湖廣。

translations.literal: Before long Zhidong was transferred to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhidong became governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 之洞既移鄂，益銳意興辦盧漢鐵路，其所經畫，曰儲材宜急，勘路宜緩，興工宜遲，竣工宜速。

translations.literal: After Zhidong moved to E, he was all the more determined to undertake the Lu-Han railway; what he planned was: storing materials should be urgent, surveying the route should be slow, starting work should be late, and completion should be swift.
translations.idiomatic: In Hubei he pressed Lu-Han with a maxim: stock materials quickly, survey slowly, start late, finish fast.

sentences.zh: 以商股難恃，請歲撥帑金二百萬兩以備路用。

translations.literal: Because merchant shares were hard to rely on, he requested two million taels of treasury silver annually to prepare for road expenses.
translations.idiomatic: With merchant capital unreliable, he sought two million taels yearly from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 上如所請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以東三省邊事亟，從海軍衙門王大臣及直督李鴻章言，命移盧漢路款先辦關東鐵路。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because eastern Three Provinces border affairs were urgent, following the Naval Affairs Yamen princes and ministers and Governor-General Li Hongzhang, an order moved Lu-Han road funds to build the eastern Pass railway first.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 16, border crises in the northeast led the court to divert Lu-Han funds to a Manchurian railway first.

sentences.zh: 擬由林西造幹路，出山海關至瀋陽達吉林，另由瀋陽造枝路以至牛庄、營口，計二千三百二十三里，年撥銀二百萬兩為關東造路專★，命李鴻章為督辦大臣，裕祿為會辦大臣，而盧漢路工因之延緩。

translations.literal: It was planned to build a trunk from Linxi out through Shanhaiguan to Shenyang reaching Jilin, and separately from Shenyang build a branch to Niuzhuang and Yingkou, totaling 2,323 li, with two million taels allocated annually as dedicated funds for eastern Pass road building; Li Hongzhang was appointed superintendent minister and Yu Lu co-superintendent, while Lu-Han road work was thereby delayed.
translations.idiomatic: A 2,323-li trunk from Linxi through Shanhaiguan to Shenyang and Jilin, with branches to Niuzhuang and Yingkou, would receive two million taels yearly; Li Hongzhang and Yu Lu supervised, delaying Lu-Han.

sentences.zh: 蓋自光緒初年，內外臣工往往條陳鐵路，當國者亦欲試行以開風氣，而疆吏畏難因循，顧慮清議，莫敢為天下先。

translations.literal: From the early Guangxu reign, inner and outer officials often submitted memorials on railways; those holding state power also wished to try implementation to open custom, yet frontier officials feared difficulty and followed precedent, considering pure criticism, and none dared take the lead for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since early Guangxu, memorials had urged railways, but officials feared pioneering amid censorial attack.

sentences.zh: 盧漢鐵路已定議矣，尋復中輟。

translations.literal: The Lu-Han railway had been decided, then was again suspended midway.
translations.idiomatic: Lu-Han was agreed, then halted again.

sentences.zh: 至是年，國內鐵路，僅有唐山至閻庄八十五里，閻庄至林西鎮二百三十五里，又基隆至淡水六十里而已。

translations.literal: By this year domestic railways amounted only to Tangshan–Yanzhuang 85 li, Yanzhuang–Linxi Town 235 li, and Keelung–Tamsui 60 li.
translations.idiomatic: By then China had only 85 li Tangshan–Yanzhuang, 235 li Yanzhuang–Linxi, and 60 li Keelung–Tamsui.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命張之洞遴保人才，及籌議清江至京路事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year an order directed Zhang Zhidong to select and recommend talent and to deliberate the Qingjiang–Beijing route.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 21 the court ordered Zhang Zhidong to recommend talent and study the Qingjiang–Beijing line.

sentences.zh: 之洞言鐵路以盧漢為要，江寧、蘇、杭次之，清江築路非宜。

translations.literal: Zhidong said railways took Lu-Han as essential, Nanjing–Suzhou–Hangzhou next, and that building a line at Qingjiang was not appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong replied that Lu-Han mattered most, Nanjing–Suzhou–Hangzhou next, and Qingjiang was unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 上韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時之洞方督兩江，特命移鄂綜其事。

translations.literal: At that time Zhidong was governor-general of the Two Jiangs; he was specially ordered transferred to E to oversee the matter comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: Though then at Nanjing, he was transferred to Hubei to direct the work.

sentences.zh: 以盧漢路長款鉅，諭有招股千萬者，許設公司自辦。

translations.literal: Because the Lu-Han route was long and funds huge, an edict said whoever raised ten million in shares might establish a company to run it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The court offered a company charter to anyone raising ten million taels for Lu-Han.

sentences.zh: 粵人許應鏘、方培■J0等咸言集貲如額，遵旨承辦。

translations.literal: Guangdong men Xu Yingqiang, Fang Pei[sun], and others all said they had raised funds to quota and would undertake as ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese promoters Xu Yingqiang, Fang Pei, and others claimed the full subscription.

sentences.zh: 直督王文韶與之洞言承辦各商舉不足恃，請以津海關道盛宣懷為督辦，允之，命以四品京堂督路事。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wang Wenshao of Zhili told Zhidong that the undertaking merchants’ pledges were not reliable and requested Tianjin maritime customs intendant Sheng Xuanhuai as superintendent; approval was granted, ordering him as fourth-rank capital official to supervise road affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshao of Zhili doubted the merchants and proposed Sheng Xuanhuai as superintendent; the court agreed and appointed Sheng fourth-rank supervisor.

sentences.zh: 宣懷條上四事，一請特設鐵路總公司，撥官款，募商股，借洋債。

translations.literal: Xuanhuai submitted four items in a memorial, first requesting a special railway general company, allocating official funds, raising merchant shares, and borrowing foreign debt.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized four points: a national railway company, official funds, merchant shares, and foreign loans.

sentences.zh: 先辦盧漢，次第及於蘇滬、粵漢。

translations.literal: Build Lu-Han first, then in order extend to Suzhou–Shanghai and Guangdong–Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu-Han would come first, then Suzhou–Shanghai and Guangdong–Hankou.

sentences.zh: 上如所請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 是年設總公司於上海，而盧漢之始基以立。

translations.literal: That year the general company was established in Shanghai, and the foundation of Lu-Han was thereby laid.
translations.idiomatic: That year the company opened in Shanghai, laying Lu-Han’s foundation.

sentences.zh: 自中日戰後，外人窺伺中國益亟，侵略之策，以攬辦鐵路為先。

translations.literal: After the Sino-Japanese War, foreigners watching China grew ever more urgent; among policies of aggression, taking charge of building railways came first.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat by Japan, foreign powers eyed China more keenly, and railway concessions headed their plans.

sentences.zh: 俄索接造西伯利亞幹路，橫貫黑、吉兩省，修枝路以達旅順、大連灣。

translations.literal: Russia demanded to continue building the Siberia trunk, running across Heilongjiang and Jilin provinces, and branch lines reaching Lüshun and Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: Russia sought to extend the Trans-Siberian trunk through Heilongjiang and Jilin with branches to Lüshun and Dalian.

sentences.zh: 英則請修五路：一蘇杭甬，自蘇州經杭州以達寧波；

translations.literal: England then requested five routes: first Su-Hang-Yong, from Suzhou via Hangzhou to Ningbo;
translations.idiomatic: Britain requested five lines: first, Suzhou–Hangzhou–Ningbo from Suzhou via Hangzhou to Ningbo;

sentences.zh: 一廣九，自廣州以達九龍；

translations.literal: second Guang–Jiu, from Guangzhou to Kowloon;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Guangzhou–Kowloon line from Guangzhou to Kowloon;

sentences.zh: 一津鎮，自天津以達鎮江；

translations.literal: third Tian–Zhen, from Tianjin to Zhenjiang;
translations.idiomatic: third, the Tianjin–Zhenjiang line from Tianjin to Zhenjiang;

sentences.zh: 一浦信，自浦口以達信陽；

translations.literal: fourth Pu–Xin, from Pukou to Xinyang;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Pukou–Xinyang line from Pukou to Xinyang;

sentences.zh: 一自山西、河南以達長江。

translations.literal: fifth from Shanxi and Henan to reach the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: and Shanxi–Henan to the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 法自越南筑路以達雲南省，自龍州築路以達鎮南關。

translations.literal: France built roads from Vietnam to reach Yunnan province, and from Longzhou built roads to reach Zhennan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: France built from Vietnam into Yunnan and from Longzhou to Zhennan Pass.

sentences.zh: 德踞膠州灣，築路以達濟南。

translations.literal: Germany occupied Jiaozhou Bay and built roads to reach Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Germany held Jiaozhou and built toward Jinan.

sentences.zh: 葡據澳門，築路以達廣州。

translations.literal: Portugal held Macau and built roads to reach Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Portugal held Macau and built toward Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 日本擅於新民廳築路達奉天，更獲有奉天至安東鐵道之權。

translations.literal: Japan unilaterally built roads at Xinmin ting reaching Fengtian, and further obtained rights to the Fengtian–Andong railway.
translations.idiomatic: Japan built from Xinmin to Fengtian and gained the Fengtian–Andong line.

sentences.zh: 此各國以鐵路侵略中國之大略也。

translations.literal: This is the great outline of the various nations using railways to aggress China.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad foreign strategy of railway imperialism.

sentences.zh: 先是俄人陰結朝鮮窺奉天，建言者請急建關內外路以相鈐制，乃命順天府尹胡燏棻督辦津榆路事；

translations.literal: Earlier Russians had secretly allied with Korea and watched Fengtian; memorialists requested urgently building the inside-and-outside Pass route to check and restrain them, and therefore Shuntian prefect Hu Jia’en was ordered to supervise Tianjin–Yulin road affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Russia courted Korea and eyed Fengtian, memorialists urged a railway through the Pass; Shuntian prefect Hu Jia’en supervised the Tianjin–Yulin line;

sentences.zh: 後以續造吉林一路款絀中輟。

translations.literal: later because funds for continuing Jilin route were insufficient it was again suspended midway.
translations.idiomatic: later the Jilin extension halted for lack of funds.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，俄事急，燏棻請息借英款為之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, with Russian affairs urgent, Jia’en requested resting on borrowed English funds to build it.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24, with Russia pressing, Hu Jia’en sought an English loan.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「關外一路，初擬逕達吉林，以無款又落後著。

translations.literal: He memorialized: “The route beyond the Pass was first planned to reach Jilin directly; because there were no funds it again fell behind.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that the northeastern trunk to Jilin had stalled for lack of money;

sentences.zh: 迨歸併津盧，俄即起而爭執。

translations.literal: when it was merged into Tianjin–Lushun, Russia immediately rose to contend.
translations.idiomatic: merging it with Tianjin–Lushun had provoked Russian claims;

sentences.zh: 近允其由俄邊直接大連灣，奉、吉兩省東北之利盡為所佔。

translations.literal: Recently permission was given for them to go directly from the Russian border to Dalian Bay, and the benefits of the northeast of Feng and Ji provinces were entirely occupied by them.
translations.idiomatic: Russia was now allowed a direct line to Dalian, dominating eastern Liaoning and Jilin;

sentences.zh: 計惟有由大凌河趕造至新民廳鐵路，以備聯絡瀋陽之路，並可兼護蒙古、熱河礦務。

translations.literal: The plan can only be to hurry building a railway from Daling River to Xinmin ting to prepare linking the route to Shenyang, and it can also protect Mongol and Rehe mining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: China must rush a line from Daling River to Xinmin to link Shenyang and guard Mongol and Rehe mining;

sentences.zh: 一面由營口至廣寧，庶中國海關不致為俄侵佔，尚可保全奉省西北之利。

translations.literal: On one side from Yingkou to Guangning, so that Chinese maritime customs will not be invaded and occupied by Russia, and the northwest benefits of Feng province may still be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: and build Yingkou–Guangning so customs and northwestern Liaoning might be saved.

sentences.zh: 現東三省全局已在俄人掌握，幸留此一線之路，堪以設法抵禦。

translations.literal: At present the overall situation of the Three Eastern Provinces is already in Russian hands; fortunately this one thread of road remains, by which one may devise methods to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The northeast was largely lost to Russia, but this slender railway might still resist;

sentences.zh: 若坐失機宜，後悔何及。

translations.literal: If one sits and loses the opportune moment, what regret will there be afterward?
translations.idiomatic: delay would bring irreparable regret.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，英人圖粵路甚亟。

translations.literal: Earlier the English had schemed for the Guangdong route very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Britain had long coveted the Guangdong railway.

sentences.zh: 王文韶、張之洞、盛宣懷合疏言：「粵漢南幹路，原擬稍緩續籌，無如時局日亟，刻不及待。

translations.literal: Wang Wenshao, Zhang Zhidong, and Sheng Xuanhuai jointly memorialized: “The Guangdong–Hankou southern trunk was originally planned to be raised and funded more slowly; but the situation daily grows urgent and the moment cannot wait.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, Zhang, and Sheng jointly urged that the Guangdong–Hankou southern trunk could no longer wait;

sentences.zh: 群雄環伺，輒以交涉細故，兵輪互相馳騁，海洋通塞，靡有定期。

translations.literal: Powerful states surround and watch; they often use minor diplomatic pretexts while warships race one another; whether the seas are open or blocked has no fixed period.
translations.idiomatic: powers circled China, warships prowled, and sea lanes were insecure;

sentences.zh: 今海軍既無力能興，設有外變，隔若異域，必內地造有鐵路，方可聯絡貫通。

translations.literal: Now the navy has no strength to revive; if there is external change, separated as if a different region, inland railways must be built before one can link and penetrate through.
translations.idiomatic: without a navy, only inland railways could connect the empire in crisis;

sentences.zh: 廣東財賦之區，南戒山河，未可遐棄，此粵漢南路當與北路並舉者也。

translations.literal: Guangdong is a region of state wealth and revenue, south guarded by mountains and rivers—it cannot be cast far away; therefore the Guangdong–Hankou southern route should be undertaken together with the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong’s wealth and strategic rivers required building the southern trunk alongside the northern.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「德國無理肇釁，占踞膠、墨要害，並獲承辦山東鐵路。

translations.literal: ” They also memorialized: “Germany without reason began trouble, occupied the strategic points of Jiao and Mo, and also obtained undertaking Shandong railways.
translations.idiomatic: They added that Germany had seized Jiaozhou and won Shandong railways;

sentences.zh: 俄已造路於黑龍江、吉林，為通奉天、旅順之謀。

translations.literal: Russia has already built roads in Heilongjiang and Jilin as a plan to reach Fengtian and Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: Russia was building through Heilongjiang and Jilin toward Fengtian and Lüshun;

sentences.zh: 法已造路於廣西，以為割滇之計。

translations.literal: France has already built roads in Guangxi as a plan to carve off Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: France was building in Guangxi toward Yunnan;

sentences.zh: 獨英人窺伺最久，尚無所得。

translations.literal: Only the English, who have watched longest, have still obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: only Britain had yet gained its prize.

sentences.zh: 今年春，英商屢來攬辦粵路，堅持未允。

translations.literal: This spring English merchants repeatedly came to undertake the Guangdong route, and held firmly to refusal.
translations.idiomatic: That spring British merchants repeatedly sought the Guangdong line and were refused.

sentences.zh: 其所擬急行者，在趕營中國中部，或廣東建築軌道。

translations.literal: What they urgently intend is to hurry to operate in central China, or to build track in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Britain now aimed at central China or Guangdong track.

sentences.zh: 蓋英所欲者，一借款，一修路，一擬索香港對岸之深水埠，其為覬覦鐵路無疑。

translations.literal: What England desires is one—loans, one—building roads, one—planning to demand the deep-water port opposite Hong Kong; there is no doubt of its coveting railways.
translations.idiomatic: Britain wanted loans, railways, and a deep-water port opposite Hong Kong—clearly targeting rail rights.

sentences.zh: 現在德已踞膠，俄已留旅，法已窺瓊，英有圖扼長江、吳淞之謀。

translations.literal: Now Germany has already occupied Jiao, Russia has already retained Lü, France already watches Qiong; England has a plan to choke the Yangtze and Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: Germany held Jiaozhou, Russia Lüshun, France Hainan, while Britain eyed the Yangtze and Wusong.

sentences.zh: 是中國各海口幾盡為外國所佔，僅有內地尚可南北往來。

translations.literal: This is that China's various sea ports are nearly all occupied by foreign countries; only the interior can still travel north and south.
translations.idiomatic: China's seaports were nearly all in foreign hands; only the interior still allowed north–south movement.

sentences.zh: 若粵漢一線再假手英人，將來俄路南引，英軌北趨，惟有盧漢一路跼蹐其中，何能展布？

translations.literal: If the Guangdong–Hankou line is again placed in English hands, in future when the Russian road leads south and the English track presses north, there will be only the Lu-Han route cramped within—how can it expand and deploy?
translations.idiomatic: If Britain built Guangdong–Hankou while Russia pushed south and Britain north, Lu-Han would be trapped between them.

sentences.zh: 甚或為英、俄之路所並。

translations.literal: It might even be merged by English and Russian roads.
translations.idiomatic: It might even be absorbed into Anglo-Russian lines.

sentences.zh: 惟有趕將粵漢一路占定自辦，尚足補救萬一。

translations.literal: Only by hurrying to secure the Guangdong–Hankou route for self-management can one still remedy the situation by one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: Only by securing Guangdong–Hankou for Chinese operation could the danger be partly averted.

sentences.zh: 」嘉納之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 初，粵漢路議由鄂入贛達粵。

translations.literal: Earlier the Guangdong–Hankou route proposal went from E into Gan to reach Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong–Hankou line was first planned from Hubei through Jiangxi to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 嗣病其迂遠，改道湘之郴、永、衡、長。

translations.literal: Later, finding it too circuitous, the route was changed through Hunan's Chen, Yong, Heng, and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: It was later rerouted through Chenzhou, Yongzhou, Hengyang, and Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 至是，定議三省紳商自辦，總公司綜其綱領。

translations.literal: By this time it was decided that gentry and merchants of the three provinces would undertake it themselves, with the general company overseeing the overall plan.
translations.idiomatic: The three provinces' gentry and merchants would build it under a parent company.

sentences.zh: 蓋各省幹路，以關東肇其端，盧漢、粵漢次之。

translations.literal: Generally among provincial trunk lines, the eastern Pass began first, then Lu-Han and Guangdong–Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Among trunk lines, the northeast came first, then Lu-Han and Guangdong–Hankou.

sentences.zh: 此外則建天津至盧溝橋之津盧路，正定至太原之正太路，鄭州東至開封、西曆滎陽、汜水達洛陽之汴洛路，廣州至九龍之廣九路，上海至江寧之滬寧路，萍鄉至昭山之萍昭路，道口至清化鎮之道清路，京師至張家口之京張路，天津至浦口之津浦路，吉林、長春之吉長路，齊齊哈爾卜魁城至昂昂溪之齊昂路，此屬於官辦者也。

translations.literal: Besides these were built the Tianjin–Lugouqiao Jing-Lu line, Zhengding–Taiyuan Zheng-Tai line, Zhengzhou east to Kaifeng and west through Xingyang and Sishui to Luoyang Bian-Luo line, Guangzhou to Kowloon Guang-Jiu line, Shanghai to Jiangning Hu-Ning line, Pingxiang to Zhaoshan Ping-Zhao line, Daokou to Qinghua Town Dao-Qing line, capital to Zhangjiakou Jing-Zhang line, Tianjin to Pukou Jin-Pu line, Jilin–Changchun Ji-Chang line, Qiqihar Buque City to Angangxi Qi-Ang line—these belong to government operation.
translations.idiomatic: Government lines included Jing-Lu, Zheng-Tai, Bian-Luo, Guang-Jiu, Hu-Ning, Ping-Zhao, Dao-Qing, Jing-Zhang, Jin-Pu, Ji-Chang, and Qi-Ang, among others.

sentences.zh: 若潮汕、新寧、川漢、同蒲、洛潼、西潼、廣廈、歸包、歸新、桂全、滇桂、滇蜀、騰越以及浙、蘇、皖、贛、滇、蜀諸省，咸請自修幹枝等路，悉如所請。

translations.literal: Such as Chao-Shan, Xinning, Chuan-Han, Tong-Pu, Luo-Tong, Xi-Tong, Guang-Xia, Gui-Bao, Gui-Xin, Gui-Quan, Dian-Gui, Dian-Shu, Tengyue, and the provinces Zhe, Su, Wan, Gan, Dian, and Shu—all requested to build their own trunk and branch lines, and all were approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial requests to build local trunk and branch lines—including Chao-Shan, Sichuan–Hankou, and many others—were generally approved.

sentences.zh: 至是建造鐵路之說，風行全國，自朝廷以逮士庶，咸以鐵路為當務之急。

translations.literal: By this time the talk of building railways swept the whole country; from the court down to commoners, all regarded railways as the most urgent task of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Railway building became a national obsession from court to populace.

sentences.zh: 趨鄉既定，籌款與辦法最關緊要。

translations.literal: Once the route was set, raising funds and methods of operation were most closely related and important.
translations.idiomatic: Once routes were chosen, financing and management mattered most.

sentences.zh: 籌款有官帑，有洋債，有民股。

translations.literal: Raising funds had official treasury funds, foreign debt, and popular shares.
translations.idiomatic: Funding came from the treasury, foreign loans, or private shares.

sentences.zh: 修路有官辦，有商辦，有官督商辦。

translations.literal: Building roads had government operation, merchant operation, and government-supervised merchant operation.
translations.idiomatic: Construction could be official, private, or government-supervised private.

sentences.zh: 自劉銘傳倡借債築路之議，為眾論所尼，借款修路，遂為當時所諱言。

translations.literal: From Liu Mingchuan's advocacy of borrowing debt to build roads being obstructed by public opinion, borrowing to build roads became what was taboo to speak of at the time.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Mingchuan's loan proposal was shouted down, foreign loans became politically toxic.

sentences.zh: 故盧漢建議之初，猶以部帑為請，未敢昌言借洋債也。

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of the Lu-Han proposal they still requested ministry funds and did not dare speak openly of borrowing foreign debt.
translations.idiomatic: Lu-Han initially sought only official funds, not foreign debt.

sentences.zh: 借洋債自津盧、關內外鐵路始。

translations.literal: Borrowing foreign debt began with the Tianjin–Lushun and inside-and-outside Pass railways.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign railway loans began with Tianjin–Lushun and the Manchurian lines.

sentences.zh: 迨盛宣懷督辦路事，首以三路分三國借款之策進。

translations.literal: When Sheng Xuanhuai supervised road affairs, he first advanced the policy of three routes borrowing from three nations.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Xuanhuai proposed borrowing from three countries for three lines.

sentences.zh: 曰盧漢借比款，滬寧借英款，粵漢借美款。

translations.literal: Namely Lu-Han borrowing Belgian funds, Hu-Ning borrowing English funds, Guangdong–Hankou borrowing American funds.
translations.idiomatic: Lu-Han would take Belgian money, Hu-Ning British, Guangdong–Hankou American.

sentences.zh: 上俞其請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是正太則借俄款，汴洛則借比款，廣九、蘇杭甬則借英款，津浦則借英、德款。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng-Tai borrowed Russian funds, Bian-Luo Belgian funds, Guang-Jiu and Su-Hang-Yong English funds, Jin-Pu English and German funds.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng-Tai followed with Russian loans, Bian-Luo Belgian, Guang-Jiu and Su-Hang-Yong British, Jin-Pu Anglo-German.

sentences.zh: 貸之者，大率資金什予其九，息金二什而取其一；

translations.literal: Those who lent, for the most part supplied nine-tenths of the capital and took one-tenth as interest;
translations.idiomatic: Lenders typically supplied nine-tenths of capital and charged interest of one part in twenty;

sentences.zh: 以路為質，或並及附路之產物。

translations.literal: taking the railway as collateral, or also including products of attached routes.
translations.idiomatic: the railway, or its ancillary assets, served as security.

sentences.zh: 付息、還本、贖路，咸有定程，而還本、贖路未及其時，且勿許。

translations.literal: Paying interest, repaying principal, and redeeming the road all had fixed schedules, and before the time for repaying principal or redeeming the road, it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Interest, principal, and buyback followed fixed schedules with no early redemption.

sentences.zh: 購料、勘路、興工，多假外人為之。

translations.literal: Purchasing materials, surveying routes, and starting work were mostly done by foreigners on loan.
translations.idiomatic: Materials, surveys, and construction were largely foreign-run.

sentences.zh: 故外人多以款為餌，冀獲承辦之利。

translations.literal: Therefore foreigners often used funds as bait, hoping to obtain the profit of undertaking construction.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners used loans as bait for construction contracts.

sentences.zh: 盧漢路近三千里，費逾四千萬，黃河橋工糜款尤鉅，官帑僅資開辦而已。

translations.literal: The Lu-Han route was nearly three thousand li, costing more than forty million; the Yellow River bridge work especially consumed funds hugely—official funds only supplied startup.
translations.idiomatic: Lu-Han, nearly three thousand li and over forty million taels, relied on official funds only to start; the Yellow River bridge consumed most.

sentences.zh: 借款始擬美，以所望奢，改與比議。

translations.literal: Borrowing was first planned from America; because their demands were extravagant, it was changed to negotiation with Belgium.
translations.idiomatic: A U.S. loan was first sought but rejected as too costly; Belgium won the contract.

sentences.zh: 英、德、法諸國接踵而至。

translations.literal: England, Germany, France, and other nations arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Britain, Germany, and France also competed.

sentences.zh: 卒借比款一百十二兆五十萬佛郎。

translations.literal: In the end Belgian funds of 112,050,000 francs were borrowed.
translations.idiomatic: Belgium lent 112,050,000 francs.

sentences.zh: 比小國，饒鋼鐵，嫺工事，於中國無大志。

translations.literal: Belgium is a small state, rich in steel and iron, skilled in engineering, with no great ambition toward China.
translations.idiomatic: Belgium, small but skilled in steel and engineering, seemed less threatening.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，續借一百二十五萬佛郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year an additional 1,250,000 francs was borrowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 31 another 1,250,000 francs was borrowed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，路成。

translations.literal: The next year the road was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The line opened the following year.

sentences.zh: 北端直抵京師，因易名京漢。

translations.literal: The northern end reached straight to the capital, and the name was therefore changed to Jing-Han.
translations.idiomatic: Its northern terminus reached Beijing, and it was renamed Jing-Han (Beijing–Hankou).

sentences.zh: 京漢之枝路曰正太，曰汴洛。

translations.literal: Branches of Jing-Han are called Zheng-Tai and Bian-Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Branches included Zheng-Tai and Bian-Luo.

sentences.zh: 正太借款，始二十三年。

translations.literal: Zheng-Tai borrowing began in the twenty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng-Tai loans began in Guangxu 23.

sentences.zh: 俄璞科第與晉官紳議定而中止。

translations.literal: Russian Pokotdi negotiated with Shanxi officials and gentry and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Russian agent Pokotdi negotiated with Shanxi elites, then stalled.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，盛宣懷與議借款四千萬佛郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Sheng Xuanhuai negotiated borrowing forty million francs.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 28 Sheng negotiated forty million francs.

sentences.zh: 約成，而俄人挨士巴尼忽索太原至榆次，至成都，至太谷，至西安，石庄至東光、微水、橫澗四岔道，及同蒲諸路。

translations.literal: When the contract was made, Russians suddenly demanded Taiyuan to Yuci, to Chengdu, to Taigu, to Xi'an, Shijiazhuang to Dongguang, Weishui, Hengjian four branch lines, and the Tong-Pu routes.
translations.idiomatic: Once contracted, Russia demanded branches to Chengdu, Xi'an, and elsewhere, plus Tong-Pu lines.

sentences.zh: 均格部議，而岔道卒如所請。

translations.literal: All were blocked by ministry deliberation, yet the branch lines in the end were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry resisted, but branches were granted as Russia asked.

sentences.zh: 三十三年秋，工竣。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirty-third year the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Work finished in autumn of Guangxu 33.

sentences.zh: 自容閎倡辦津鎮，盛宣懷恐奪盧漢之利，因議辦汴洛、開濟以相鈐制。

translations.literal: From Rong Hong's advocacy of Jin-Zhen, Sheng Xuanhuai feared losing Lu-Han profit and therefore proposed Bian-Luo and Kaiji to check and restrain.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong Hong's Jin-Zhen proposal, Sheng countered with Bian-Luo and Kaiji to protect Lu-Han.

sentences.zh: 汴洛借款始於二十五年，至二十八年而約成，借比款二千五百萬佛郎。

translations.literal: Bian-Luo borrowing began in the twenty-fifth year; by the twenty-eighth year the contract was made, borrowing Belgian funds of 25,000,000 francs.
translations.idiomatic: Bian-Luo loans began in Guangxu 25; the 25-million-franc contract closed in Guangxu 28.

sentences.zh: 比人盧法爾主工事。

translations.literal: Belgian Laffont directed the engineering work.
