translations.idiomatic: Belgian engineer Laffont directed construction.

sentences.zh: 嗣續借千六百萬佛郎。

translations.literal: Later an additional 16,000,000 francs was borrowed.
translations.idiomatic: Another 16 million francs followed.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，路成。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year the road was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The line opened in Guangxu 34.

sentences.zh: 津沽用款百三十萬，官帑、商股兼備，以洋債補其不足。

translations.literal: Jingu used 1,300,000 in funds, with official treasury and merchant shares both prepared, using foreign debt to supplement the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin line cost 1.3 million, mixing official and merchant funds with foreign loans.

sentences.zh: 津盧假英金四十萬鎊。

translations.literal: Tianjin–Lushun borrowed 400,000 pounds sterling.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin–Lushun borrowed £400,000.

sentences.zh: 關內外路借英金二百三十萬鎊。

translations.literal: The inside-and-outside Pass route borrowed £2,300,000 sterling.
translations.idiomatic: The Manchurian railway borrowed £2.3 million.

sentences.zh: 本由商辦，迨胡燏棻為督辦，始官為之。

translations.literal: Originally merchant-run; when Hu Jia'en became superintendent, the government took it over.
translations.idiomatic: It began as merchant-built; Hu Jia'en made it official.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂起，關外路為俄踞，關內路為英踞。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, the route beyond the Pass was occupied by Russia and the route within by England.
translations.idiomatic: During the Boxer crisis Russia seized the outer line and Britain the inner.

sentences.zh: 命袁世凱等與英使立約收回，英人遂攫有百里內不准他人承修之權。

translations.literal: Yuan Shikai and others were ordered to conclude a treaty with the English minister to recover it; the English then seized the right that within a hundred li no others might undertake construction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shikai negotiated recovery, but Britain won a hundred-li monopoly on new construction.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，全路告竣，是為京奉路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the whole route was reported complete—this is the Jing-Feng route.
translations.idiomatic: The full Jing-Feng (Beijing–Fengtian) line opened in Guangxu 31.

sentences.zh: 道清路為英商福公司所造，長九十里，利微費鉅。

translations.literal: The Dao-Qing route was built by the English Fu Company, ninety li in length, small profit and huge expense.
translations.idiomatic: The ninety-li Dao-Qing line, built by Britain's Fu Company, lost money heavily.

sentences.zh: 初，英商索澤襄、懷浦，俱不獲。

translations.literal: Earlier the English merchant sought Ze-Xiang and Huai-Pu but obtained neither.
translations.idiomatic: Britain had earlier sought Ze-Xiang and Huai-Pu routes in vain.

sentences.zh: 遂以借款收回道清為言，內外臣工咸持不可，終借英金六十一萬四千六百鎊贖回。

translations.literal: Then they spoke of recovering Dao-Qing by loan; inner and outer officials all held it impossible, yet in the end £614,600 was borrowed to redeem it.
translations.idiomatic: Britain offered to return Dao-Qing for a loan; officials resisted, but £614,600 redeemed it.

sentences.zh: 津浦路，因津鎮之議不果行，改議北起天津，南訖浦口，借英、德款五百萬鎊。

translations.literal: The Jin-Pu route, because the Jin-Zhen proposal did not succeed, was changed to debate north from Tianjin and south ending at Pukou, borrowing English and German funds of five million pounds.
translations.idiomatic: Jin-Pu, replacing failed Jin-Zhen, ran Tianjin to Pukou on £5 million Anglo-German loans.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂海寰主其事。

translations.literal: Minister Lü Haihuan directed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lü Haihuan supervised it.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，工竣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: It opened in Xuantong 3.

sentences.zh: 其促成各省鐵路自辦與拒絕外債之機者，則滬寧、蘇杭甬、粵漢借款所致也。

translations.literal: What prompted provincial self-built railways and refusal of foreign debt was caused by Hu-Ning, Su-Hang-Yong, and Guangdong–Hankou borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial self-build movements and anti-foreign-loan sentiment stemmed from Hu-Ning, Su-Hang-Yong, and Guangdong–Hankou loans.

sentences.zh: 滬寧築路，倡於盛宣懷，南北洋大臣據以入告，得請。

translations.literal: Hu-Ning railway building was initiated by Sheng Xuanhuai; the northern and southern sea governors reported upward on this basis and obtained approval.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Xuanhuai proposed Hu-Ning; coastal governors secured approval.

sentences.zh: 方從事淞滬工作，而英聲請承辦，宣懷與訂草約。

translations.literal: Just as work on the Songhu section was underway, the English requested to undertake it; Xuanhuai signed a draft contract with them.
translations.idiomatic: During Songhu construction Britain sought the contract; Sheng signed a draft.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，正約成，借英金三百二十五萬鎊，五十年為期。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the formal contract was made, borrowing £3,250,000 sterling, fifty years as term.
translations.idiomatic: The formal contract in Guangxu 29 borrowed £3.25 million for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 商部以借款幾倍於原估之數詰之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Commerce questioned that the loan was several times the original estimate.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Commerce protested that the loan far exceeded estimates.

sentences.zh: 而工未及半，款已告罄，復議續借百萬鎊。

translations.literal: Yet before half the work was done the funds were exhausted, and renewed debate proposed borrowing another million pounds.
translations.idiomatic: Before half was built, funds ran out and another £1 million was sought.

sentences.zh: 蘇人群起責難，並疏聞於上。

translations.literal: The people of Su rose in mass to blame and also memorialized the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu public outrage reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 命唐紹儀督辦滬寧、京漢，罷鐵路總公司。

translations.literal: Tang Shaoyi was ordered to supervise Hu-Ning and Jing-Han and abolish the railway general company.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shaoyi replaced Sheng, supervising Hu-Ning and Jing-Han and dissolving the general company.

sentences.zh: 紹儀既任事，徇英工程司之請，復議售小票六十五萬鎊。

translations.literal: After Shaoyi took office, yielding to the English chief engineer's request, renewed debate proposed selling debentures of £650,000.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, pressed by British engineers, proposed £650,000 in new debentures.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「盛宣懷移交合同文卷及購地工程帳冊，支款浮濫，當經駁回。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Sheng Xuanhuai handed over contract documents and land purchase and engineering account books; expenditures were inflated and were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Tang reported that Sheng's contracts and accounts showed inflated spending he had rejected.

sentences.zh: 滬寧合同吃虧，比京漢幹路為甚。

translations.literal: The Hu-Ning contract suffered losses, worse than the Jing-Han trunk.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu-Ning contract was more ruinous than Jing-Han.

sentences.zh: 其最棘手者，在設立總管理處。

translations.literal: The most difficult point lies in establishing a general management office.
translations.idiomatic: Worst was the general management office.

sentences.zh: 華員二人，洋員三人，每會議時，彼眾我寡，已佔低著。

translations.literal: Two Chinese members, three foreign members—at each meeting they were many and we few, already occupying the lower position.
translations.idiomatic: Two Chinese and three foreigners met; foreigners always outvoted Chinese.

sentences.zh: 議者有添舉監督之說。

translations.literal: Some who debated proposed adding supervisory posts.
translations.idiomatic: Some suggested adding supervisors.

sentences.zh: 豈知權在總管理處，合同早已訂明，雖有監督，實不濟事。

translations.literal: They did not know that power lay in the general management office; the contract had long been fixed—though there were supervisors, in fact they could not help.
translations.idiomatic: But the contract fixed power in the office; supervisors were powerless.

sentences.zh: 其尤棘手者，財政之權操于洋人掌握，用款雖由華員簽字，而司帳者為洋員也。

translations.literal: The especially difficult point: fiscal authority was held in foreign hands; though Chinese signed expenditures, the accountants were foreign members.
translations.idiomatic: Finance rested with foreign accountants despite Chinese signatures.

sentences.zh: 分段司帳，其支發權仍在工程司也。

translations.literal: Section accountants—the power to disburse still lay with the chief engineer.
translations.idiomatic: Section accountants still answered to foreign chief engineers.

sentences.zh: 購料事宜，向由怡和洋行經手。

translations.literal: Purchasing materials was always handled by Jardine Matheson.
translations.idiomatic: Jardine Matheson monopolized materials.

sentences.zh: 行車總管、材料總管，皆洋員專司也。

translations.literal: Traffic superintendent and materials superintendent were all exclusively managed by foreign members.
translations.idiomatic: Operations and materials chiefs were foreigners.

sentences.zh: 本彼眾我寡之因，以成事事掣肘之果。

translations.literal: Because they were many and we few, the result was hindrance at every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign majorities produced constant obstruction.

sentences.zh: 挽回補救之術，惟有改訂總管理處章程，加派華員司帳，並分任各總管，現已分別辦理。

translations.literal: The method of recovery and remedy is only to revise the general management office regulations, add Chinese accountants, and also divide responsibility among superintendents—this is already being handled separately.
translations.idiomatic: Remedies included revising regulations and appointing Chinese accountants.

sentences.zh: 至路款不敷，尚擬續售小票六十五萬鎊以資接濟。

translations.literal: As for road funds falling short, it is still planned to continue selling debentures of £650,000 to supply connection.
translations.idiomatic: Another £650,000 in debentures was still proposed to cover shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 」下所司議行。

translations.literal: " It was sent down to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 方紹儀擬續借英款也，侍郎吳郁生上疏力爭，略言：「滬寧鐵路由英國銀公司要求承造，盛宣懷與之訂立合同。

translations.literal: Just as Shaoyi was planning to continue borrowing English funds, Vice Minister Wu Yusheng submitted a memorial arguing forcefully, briefly saying: "The Hu-Ning railway was requested to be undertaken by the English bank company; Sheng Xuanhuai concluded a contract with them.
translations.idiomatic: As Tang sought more British loans, Vice Minister Wu Yusheng protested that Sheng had bound Hu-Ning to a British bank.

sentences.zh: 以長不逾六百里之路工，借款至三百五十萬鎊之鉅，估價多，必至浮濫。

translations.literal: For a route work not exceeding six hundred li in length, borrowing reached the huge sum of £3,500,000; with high estimates, there must be inflation.
translations.idiomatic: A line under six hundred li had borrowed £3.5 million—surely inflated.

sentences.zh: 自合同宣布後，遠近駭然。

translations.literal: After the contract was announced, near and far were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Public alarm followed the contract's announcement.

sentences.zh: 上年奉嚴旨改派唐紹儀妥籌辦理。

translations.literal: Last year a stern edict ordered Tang Shaoyi to arrange matters properly.
translations.idiomatic: The court had ordered Tang to fix the mess.

sentences.zh: 近聞滬寧工程司來京，又以工款不敷，有議續售小票七十萬鎊之說。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that the Hu-Ning chief engineer came to the capital, and because engineering funds fall short there is talk of continuing to sell debentures of £700,000.
translations.idiomatic: Now the British engineer sought another £700,000 in debentures.

sentences.zh: 此項路工，即就業經借定之三百五十萬鎊侭數開支，每里合銀三萬兩以上，視他路浮逾兩倍，公家受虧已多。

translations.literal: For this route work, even if the already borrowed £3,500,000 is fully spent, each li averages more than thirty thousand taels of silver, exceeding other routes by more than double in inflation—the public treasury suffers loss already greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Even the existing £3.5 million averaged over thirty thousand taels per li—more than double other lines.

sentences.zh: 今若再借鉅債，是唐紹儀接辦以來，於盛宣懷失算之處並無補救之方。

translations.literal: If now another huge debt is borrowed, then since Tang Shaoyi took over, there is no remedy for Sheng Xuanhuai's miscalculations.
translations.idiomatic: More debt would mean Tang had not corrected Sheng's errors.

sentences.zh: 請飭按照合同，嚴覈用款，一面自行籌款接濟。

translations.literal: We request ordering strict audit of expenditures according to the contract, while on one side raising funds oneself to supply connection.
translations.idiomatic: Wu urged strict audits and Chinese fundraising instead.

sentences.zh: 不可再令銀公司出售小票，致以九折虛數，受人盤剝。

translations.literal: One must not again let the bank company sell debentures, causing nine-tenth face value and suffering people's exploitation.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade further bank debenture sales at ruinous discounts.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，下所司知之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, it was sent down to the responsible offices for notice.
translations.idiomatic: The throne noted Wu's memorial.

sentences.zh: 而滬寧鐵路終以本息過鉅，收贖無期也。

translations.literal: Yet the Hu-Ning railway in the end, because principal and interest were too huge, had no date for redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Hu-Ning was never redeemed—interest and principal were too vast.

sentences.zh: 蘇杭甬鐵路，自二十四年許英商承辦。

translations.literal: The Su-Hang-Yong railway, from the twenty-fourth year, permitted English merchants to undertake it.
translations.idiomatic: Su-Hang-Yong had been promised to Britain since Guangxu 24.

sentences.zh: 是年，盛宣懷與訂草約，大要悉本滬寧。

translations.literal: That year Sheng Xuanhuai concluded a draft contract with them, the main points all following Hu-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's draft mirrored Hu-Ning's terms.

sentences.zh: 約成而英人置之。

translations.literal: When the contract was made the English put it aside.
translations.idiomatic: Britain then ignored the contract.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，浙路自辦之局定，御史硃錫恩請廢前約，上命宣懷偕浙撫主其事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the Zhejiang self-built bureau was fixed; Censor Zhu Xien requested abolishing the former contract; the emperor ordered Xuanhuai together with the Zhe governor to direct the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 31 Zhejiang chose self-build; Censor Zhu Xien sought to void the old contract; Sheng and the Zhe governor were assigned.

sentences.zh: 英人恃有前約，堅欲承辦，往復辨難要挾，久之不決。

translations.literal: The English relied on the former contract and insisted on undertaking; back and forth they argued and coerced, long undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Britain clung to the old contract; negotiations stalled for years.

sentences.zh: 侍郎汪大燮與議，分修路、借款為二事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Daxie negotiated, separating road building and borrowing into two matters.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Daxie split construction from borrowing in negotiations.

sentences.zh: 浙人以路股集有成數，一意拒款，聞之大譁，詆大燮甚力。

translations.literal: The people of Zhe, because road shares had been collected to a fixed amount, were determined to refuse loans; when they heard of this there was great uproar, and they reviled Wang Daxie very forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe investors, having subscribed shares, refused foreign loans; public outcry fiercely attacked Wang Daxie.

sentences.zh: 大燮旋使英，以梁敦彥繼之。

translations.literal: Wang Daxie soon went as envoy to England, and Liang Dunyan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was sent to Britain; Liang Dunyan took over negotiations.

sentences.zh: 浙推孫廷翰、蘇推王同愈等議於京，終以成約難廢，由部借英款，貸之兩省而事息。

translations.literal: Zhe pushed Sun Tinghan and Su pushed Wang Tongyu and others to deliberate in the capital; in the end because the completed contract was hard to void, the ministry borrowed English funds and lent them to the two provinces, and the affair subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing talks failed to void the contract; the ministry borrowed British funds and lent them to Zhejiang and Jiangsu to settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 粵漢借用美款，倡於盛宣懷。

translations.literal: Guangdong–Hankou borrowing American funds was initiated by Sheng Xuanhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Xuanhuai pioneered the American loan for Guangdong–Hankou.

sentences.zh: 駐美使伍廷芳與合興公司議借美金四千萬，期以五年工竣。

translations.literal: Minister to the United States Wu Tingfang negotiated with the American China Development Company to borrow forty million U.S. dollars, with completion of work in five years.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Wu Tingfang negotiated a $40 million loan from the China Development Company for five years' construction.

sentences.zh: 美以畢來斯司路事。

translations.literal: The Americans appointed Bliss to manage road affairs.
translations.idiomatic: American engineer Bliss directed the project.

sentences.zh: 起粵之三水，築路十五里，糜款逾二百萬。

translations.literal: Starting from Sanshui in Guangdong, fifteen li of road were built, consuming more than two million in funds.
translations.idiomatic: From Sanshui in Guangdong they built fifteen li at a cost exceeding two million.

sentences.zh: 畢來斯歿，工事亦輟，而美股多售之比人。

translations.literal: Bliss died, engineering also stopped, and most American shares were sold to Belgians.
translations.idiomatic: After Bliss died work halted, and most American shares passed to Belgians.

sentences.zh: 鄂督張之洞以比已承修盧漢，粵漢再假之比，兩路相合，非國之利，力倡廢美約之議，湘人助之。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhang Zhidong of E said that since Belgium already undertook Lu-Han, if Guangdong–Hankou were again lent to Belgium the two roads joining would not benefit the state; he strongly advocated abolishing the American contract, and Hunan people assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong argued that Belgian control of both Lu-Han and Guangdong–Hankou would harm China and led the drive to cancel the American contract, with Hunan backing him.

sentences.zh: 上用御史黃昌年言，命之洞妥籌辦理。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Censor Huang Changnian's words and ordered Zhidong to arrange matters properly.
translations.idiomatic: The throne followed Censor Huang Changnian and ordered Zhang Zhidong to handle cancellation.

sentences.zh: 之洞主廢約益力。

translations.literal: Zhidong advocated abolishing the contract ever more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang pressed harder to void the American deal.

sentences.zh: 宣懷不原，陰撓其事，詔宣懷不得干預。

translations.literal: Xuanhuai was unwilling and secretly obstructed the affair; an edict ordered Xuanhuai not to interfere.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng resisted; the court forbade him from interfering.

sentences.zh: 之洞復屬駐美使梁誠與合興公司議，年餘始定，借英金百十萬鎊贖回焉。

translations.literal: Zhidong again charged the minister to the United States Liang Cheng to negotiate with the China Development Company; after more than a year it was finally settled, borrowing £1,100,000 sterling to redeem it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had Minister Liang Cheng negotiate over a year to buy out the contract for £1.1 million.

sentences.zh: 方之洞議借英款也，英人乘間請改訂廣九路約。

translations.literal: Just as Zhidong was negotiating English borrowing, the English seized the moment to request revising the Guang-Jiu railway contract.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang arranged British funds, Britain demanded renegotiation of the Guangzhou–Kowloon line.

sentences.zh: 廣九為英人請辦五路之一，二十五年簽訂草約，懸而未定者也。

translations.literal: Guang-Jiu was one of the five routes the English requested to undertake; a draft was signed in the twenty-fifth year and left suspended undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Guang-Jiu was one of five British-requested lines; a draft signed in Guangxu 25 had lingered unsettled.

sentences.zh: 三十年，滬寧約成，英人索議未果。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the Hu-Ning contract was made; the English sought negotiation but it was not concluded.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 30, with Hu-Ning contracted, Britain again sought terms without success.

sentences.zh: 迨蘇杭甬事起，相持方急，部許英人先議廣九，以緩其事，而正約以成。

translations.literal: When the Su-Hang-Yong affair arose and stalemate was acute, the ministry permitted the English to negotiate Guang-Jiu first to ease the matter, and the formal contract was then made.
translations.idiomatic: During the Su-Hang-Yong deadlock the ministry let Britain settle Guang-Jiu first, and a formal contract followed.

sentences.zh: 至是議粵漢借款，英人復索合辦廣九全路，粵督持不可。

translations.literal: When Guangdong–Hankou borrowing was debated, the English again demanded joint undertaking of the whole Guang-Jiu route; the Guangdong governor held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangdong–Hankou loan talks Britain demanded joint control of all Guang-Jiu; the Guangdong governor refused.

sentences.zh: 旋索以粵鹽及路質借款，粵人亦不之許。

translations.literal: Soon they demanded borrowing against Guangdong salt and railway collateral; Guangdong people also did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Britain then sought loans secured on Guangdong salt and the railway; locals again refused.

sentences.zh: 終假英金百五十萬鎊而約成。

translations.literal: In the end £1,500,000 sterling was borrowed and the contract was made.
translations.idiomatic: A £1.5 million loan finally closed the Guang-Jiu contract.

sentences.zh: 之洞既借英款贖美約，一時議者以為以英易美，其害相埒，相與詬病。

translations.literal: After Zhidong borrowed English funds to redeem the American contract, opinion-makers at the time thought exchanging America for England was equally harmful, and together reviled the disease.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said swapping American for British control was equally dangerous and denounced the policy.

sentences.zh: 昌年復言路權至重，贖款難擔，亟宜興修，嚴杜干涉。

translations.literal: Changnian again said railway rights were supremely important, redemption funds hard to bear, and construction should urgently proceed while strictly blocking interference.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Changnian urged rapid construction under strict Chinese control.

sentences.zh: 詔以借款修路，流弊滋多，應由三省集股興修，以保利權。

translations.literal: An edict said borrowing to build roads had ever more flowing harms; it should be built by the three provinces collecting shares to preserve profit rights.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the three provinces to fund the line with shares, not foreign loans, to protect sovereignty.

sentences.zh: 自明詔嚴禁借債修路，而商部復有限制借款之條。

translations.literal: From the clear edict strictly forbidding borrowing debt to build roads, the Ministry of Commerce also had provisions limiting borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial bans on railway foreign debt were reinforced by commerce ministry limits on borrowing.

sentences.zh: 各省人士亦以外人謀我之亟，咸謀鐵路自辦，以杜外患，鑒外債受虧之鉅，爭欲招集股款，自保路權。

translations.literal: Provincial people also, because foreigners plotted against us urgently, all planned railways self-built to block external trouble, taking warning from the huge losses suffered on foreign debt, and vied to gather share funds to preserve road rights themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces rushed to build railways with native capital to block foreign encroachment and avoid repeating foreign-loan losses.

sentences.zh: 此由官辦改為商辦之所由來也。

translations.literal: This is the reason for the change from government operation to merchant operation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus official railways gave way to merchant-managed lines.

sentences.zh: 商辦鐵路，始於唐山至閻庄，更自天津、大沽以達林西鎮，皆開平公司為之。

translations.literal: Merchant-built railways began at Tangshan to Yanzhuang, then from Tianjin and Dagu reaching Linxi Town—all done by the Kaiping company.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant railways began with Kaiping's Tangshan–Yanzhuang line and extensions to Tianjin, Dagu, and Linxi.

sentences.zh: 嗣是武舉李福明請修京至西沽路，粵人許應鏘等請辦盧漢路，俱不獲，自此無復有言商辦者。

translations.literal: Thereafter military licentiate Li Fuming requested building from the capital to Xigu, and Guangdong men Xu Yingqiang and others requested undertaking Lu-Han—both were not obtained; from this there were no more who spoke of merchant operation.
translations.idiomatic: Later proposals by Li Fuming and Xu Yingqiang failed, and merchant initiative faded for years.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，粵人張煜南請設公司承辦潮汕鐵路。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Guangdong man Zhang Yunan requested establishing a company to undertake the Chao-Shan railway.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 29 Zhang Yunan won approval for a Chao-Shan railway company.

sentences.zh: 既得請，而川漢繼之。

translations.literal: Once approval was obtained, Sichuan–Hankou followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan–Hankou followed soon after.

sentences.zh: 川督錫良以英、美商人競涎川路，而美商班士復索灌縣富順枝路，奏准由川人籌款自辦。

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor Xi Liang, because English and American merchants competed to covet Sichuan routes, and the American Ban Shi again sought a Fushun branch at Guanxian, memorialized approval for Sichuan people to raise funds and build themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xi Liang, facing Anglo-American designs on Sichuan railways, won approval for provincial self-build.

sentences.zh: 明年，贛人以李有棻總理江西鐵路，以南潯為幹路第一段。

translations.literal: The next year Gan people took Li Youfen as general manager of the Jiangxi railway, with Nan-Xun as the first section of the trunk.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jiangxi appointed Li Youfen to begin the Nan-Xun trunk section.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，編修陳榮昌等以法人已修滇越路，滇省內地應自行推廣，以杜口實，請辦滇蜀鐵路，滇督丁振鐸據以入告，報可。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Compiler Chen Rongchang and others, because the French had already built the Yunnan–Vietnam line, said the interior of Yunnan should be extended by Chinese effort to block pretexts, and requested undertaking the Yunnan–Sichuan railway; Yunnan Governor Ding Zhenduo reported upward and received approval.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 31 Chen Rongchang urged a Yunnan–Sichuan line after the French Yunnan–Vietnam railway; Governor Ding Zhenduo secured approval.

sentences.zh: 黔撫林紹年言黔路不通，滇亦少利，因並及黔。

translations.literal: Guizhou Governor Lin Shaonian said if Guizhou routes did not connect, Yunnan would gain little profit, and therefore included Guizhou as well.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Governor Lin Shaonian added Guizhou, arguing Yunnan needed connected lines.

sentences.zh: 榮昌嗣請展修騰越，以編修吳琨總理其事。

translations.literal: Chen Rongchang later requested extending to Tengyue, with Compiler Wu Kun as general manager.
translations.idiomatic: Chen later sought extension to Tengyue under Wu Kun.

sentences.zh: 皖以李經方為總理，經始於蕪湖，以期北接盧漢、南通贛浙。

translations.literal: Anhui took Li Jingfang as general manager, beginning at Wuhu, aiming north to connect Lu-Han and south to reach Gan and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui appointed Li Jingfang to start at Wuhu, linking north to Lu-Han and south to Jiangxi and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 閩以陳寶琛為總理，築路廈門。

translations.literal: Fujian took Chen Baochen as general manager, building the route at Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian chose Chen Baochen to build from Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 浙以湯壽潛為總理，幹路一自杭達蘇，一歷富陽達江西；

translations.literal: Zhejiang took Tang Shouqian as general manager; the trunk went one from Hang to Su, one through Fuyang reaching Jiangxi;
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang's Tang Shouqian planned trunks from Hangzhou to Suzhou and through Fuyang into Jiangxi;

sentences.zh: 枝路則南道江山以通閩，西道湖、長以通皖。

translations.literal: branch routes were the southern route from Jiangshan to reach Fujian, the western route through Hu and Chang to reach Wan.
translations.idiomatic: with branches south through Jiangshan to Fujian and west through Huzhou and Changxing to Anhui.

sentences.zh: 新寧、廣廈鐵路，粵人陳宜禧、張振勛經辦。

translations.literal: Xinning and Guang-Xia railways were managed by Guangdong men Chen Yixi and Zhang Zhenxun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixi and Zhang Zhenxun managed Xinning and Guang-Xia lines in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 西潼路，近聯汴洛，遠達甘新，為西北緯幹之樞紐，陝撫曹鴻勛奏准。

translations.literal: The Xi-Tong route, near connecting Bian-Luo and far reaching Gan and Xin, was the pivot of the northwest latitudinal trunk; Shaanxi Governor Cao Hongxun memorialized approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi-Tong line, linking Bian-Luo to the northwest, was approved by Shaanxi Governor Cao Hongxun.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，蘇人以王清穆為總理，規畫江蘇全路，江南自上海經松江以達浙江，北自海州入徐以達豫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Su people took Wang Qingmu as general manager, planning the whole Jiangsu route: south of the Yangtze from Shanghai through Songjiang to Zhejiang, north from Haizhou entering Xu to reach Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 Jiangsu appointed Wang Qingmu to plan lines from Shanghai through Songjiang into Zhejiang and from Haizhou toward Henan.

sentences.zh: 桂以于式枚為總理，擬自桂林築路至全州以達湘，經梧州以達粵。

translations.literal: Gui took Yu Shimei as general manager, planning from Guilin to Quanzhou reaching Xiang, and through Wuzhou reaching Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi's Yu Shimei planned lines from Guilin to Quanzhou and Wuzhou toward Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 粵漢自美約廢后，三省公設路局於鄂，籌款築路，各自為之，不相攙越，先幹後枝，以為要約。

translations.literal: After the American Guangdong–Hankou contract was voided, the three provinces jointly established a road bureau in E, raising funds and building roads, each doing its own without mutual encroachment, trunk first then branches, as the essential agreement.
translations.idiomatic: After canceling the American contract, Hubei, Hunan, and Guangdong set a joint bureau in Hubei to build separately without overlap, trunks before branches.

sentences.zh: 湘以袁樹勛為總理，粵人內閣侍讀梁慶桂、道員黎國廉與粵督岑春煊爭粵路商辦，被劾奪官。

translations.literal: Xiang took Yuan Shuxun as general manager; Guangdong men Hanlin reader Liang Qinggui and circuit intendant Li Guoliang contended with Guangdong Governor Cen Chunxuan over merchant operation of the Guangdong route and were impeached and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan chose Yuan Shuxun; Guangdong gentry battling Governor Cen Chunxuan over merchant control were impeached.

sentences.zh: 上命往查，旋起二人原官，路由官督商辦，旬日集股數達四千萬元，以鄭官應為總理。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered investigation; soon the two men's original offices were restored; the route was government-supervised merchant operation; in ten days share subscriptions reached forty million yuan, with Zheng Guanying as general manager.
translations.idiomatic: After inquiry the gentry were restored; the line became government-supervised merchant-built; shares hit forty million yuan in ten days under Zheng Guanying.

sentences.zh: 當其時，以鐵路為救時要圖，凡有奏請，立予俞允。

translations.literal: At that time, because railways were regarded as the urgent plan to save the age, whatever was memorialized received immediate approval.
translations.idiomatic: Railway memorials received swift approval as national rescue projects.

sentences.zh: 請辦幹、枝各路，經緯相屬，幾遍全國。

translations.literal: Requests to build trunk and branch routes, warp and woof linked, spread nearly across the whole country.
translations.idiomatic: Trunk and branch proposals crisscrossed the empire.

sentences.zh: 其籌款，於招集民股外，大率不外開辦米穀、鹽、茶、房屋、彩券、土藥等捐，及銅元餘利、隨糧認股數者。

translations.literal: In raising funds, besides gathering popular shares, for the most part they were nothing beyond levies on rice and grain, salt, tea, houses, lottery tickets, native opium, and the like, and copper coin surplus profit and grain-tax share subscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Funding relied on levies on grain, salt, tea, housing, lotteries, opium, copper profits, and grain-tax share subscriptions.

sentences.zh: 而程功之速，事權之一，首推新寧。

translations.literal: For speed of completion and unity of authority, Xinning was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Xinning was fastest and most unified in authority.

sentences.zh: 陳宜禧者，籍新寧，嫺鐵路學，眾相推戴，始終其事，故二年而路竣。

translations.literal: Chen Yixi was a native of Xinning, skilled in railway learning; the multitude pushed and supported him, and he saw the affair through from start to finish—therefore the road was completed in two years.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixi of Xinning, expert in railways, led the line to completion in two years.

sentences.zh: 次則潮汕，雖勘路招股，事變屢起，而卒底於成。

translations.literal: Next was Chao-Shan; though surveying and share recruitment met repeated disturbances, in the end it was brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Chao-Shan followed, despite repeated setbacks in survey and fundraising.

sentences.zh: 總理張煜南，獎擢三品京堂。

translations.literal: General manager Zhang Yunan was rewarded and promoted to third-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunan was promoted to third-rank capital official.

sentences.zh: 此外，以粵漢路粵人集股為最多，傾軋亦最劇。

translations.literal: Besides this, Guangdong–Hankou had the most Guangdong share subscriptions, and strife was also fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong–Hankou drew the most Cantonese capital—and the fiercest infighting.

sentences.zh: 總理屢易，路工停滯。

translations.literal: General managers changed repeatedly and road work stagnated.
translations.idiomatic: Leadership churn stalled construction.

sentences.zh: 川省以租股為大宗，數達千餘萬元。

translations.literal: Sichuan relied chiefly on rent shares as the bulk, amounting to more than ten million yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan raised over ten million yuan chiefly through land rent surcharges.

sentences.zh: 浙、閩、皖、贛亦均次第興工。

translations.literal: Zhe, Min, Wan, and Gan also all began work in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang, Fujian, Anhui, and Jiangxi also started in sequence.

sentences.zh: 其餘各省，大都集股無多，有名鮮實。

translations.literal: The remaining provinces mostly gathered few shares, with name but little substance.
translations.idiomatic: Other provinces raised little beyond nominal subscriptions.

sentences.zh: 西潼一路，以商股難成，奏歸官辦，其見端也。

translations.literal: The Xi-Tong route, because merchant shares were hard to complete, memorialized return to government operation—this was how it began.
translations.idiomatic: Xi-Tong reverted to official control when merchant shares failed.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，上用蘇撫陳啟泰言，以大學士張之洞督辦粵漢，冀以統一事權，亦無所濟。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year the emperor followed Jiangsu Governor Chen Qitai's words, appointing Grand Secretary Zhang Zhidong to supervise Guangdong–Hankou, hoping thereby to unify authority—yet it also did not help.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 34 the throne put Zhang Zhidong in charge of Guangdong–Hankou to unify authority, without success.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔以鐵路為交通大政，紳商集股，各設公司，奏辦有年，多無起色，命所司遴員分往查勘。

translations.literal: That year an edict said railways were a great policy of communications; gentry and merchants gathering shares and each establishing companies had memorialized for years with little improvement; officials were ordered to select personnel to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict that year ordered inspections because share-funded companies had shown little progress.

sentences.zh: 尋奏上勘路查款辦法。

translations.literal: Soon they memorialized upward methods for surveying routes and auditing funds.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation methods for routes and funds were submitted.

sentences.zh: 時川漢已派員往查。

translations.literal: At that time Sichuan–Hankou had already sent personnel to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan–Hankou was already under review.

sentences.zh: 其餘以洛潼、西潼、同蒲、江蘇、浙江最要，為一起；

translations.literal: The rest, with Luo-Tong, Xi-Tong, Tong-Pu, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang most important, formed one group;
translations.idiomatic: Priority group one: Luo-Tong, Xi-Tong, Tong-Pu, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang;

sentences.zh: 粵漢、潮汕、新寧、惠潮、廣西、福建次要，為一起；

translations.literal: Guangdong–Hankou, Chao-Shan, Xinning, Hui-Chao, Guangxi, and Fujian secondary, formed another group;
translations.idiomatic: group two: Guangdong–Hankou, Chao-Shan, Xinning, Hui-Chao, Guangxi, and Fujian;

sentences.zh: 滇蜀、安徽、江西再次，為一起。

translations.literal: Yunnan–Sichuan, Anhui, and Jiangxi again next, formed a third group.
translations.idiomatic: group three: Yunnan–Sichuan, Anhui, and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 擬先查洛潼、西潼、同蒲三路，報聞。

translations.literal: It was planned to investigate Luo-Tong, Xi-Tong, and Tong-Pu first, and report.
translations.idiomatic: Luo-Tong, Xi-Tong, and Tong-Pu were to be inspected first.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，川路司出納者，虧倒路股百九十餘萬，川人宦京者甘大璋等聞於上，查明飭追，徒託空言而已。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong, the Sichuan railway office cashier defrauded road shares of more than 1.9 million; Sichuan officials in the capital such as Gan Dazhang heard and reported to the emperor; investigation was ordered and recovery pursued, but it was only empty words.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 a Sichuan railway cashier embezzled 1.9 million in shares; though Beijing Sichuan officials reported it, recovery proved hollow.

sentences.zh: 三年，給事中石長信言：「我國興造各省鐵路，事前並未謀定後動。

translations.literal: In the third year Giving-Remonstrance official Shi Changxin said: "Our country in building railways in the various provinces did not plan before acting.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 remonstrance official Shi Changxin said China had built railways without prior national planning.

sentences.zh: 今宜明定幹路、枝路辦法，使天下咸知國家鐵路政策之所在，此後有所遵循，不再如從前之群議龐雜，茫無主宰。

translations.literal: Now trunk and branch methods should be clearly fixed, so all under Heaven know where the state's railway policy lies; thereafter there will be something to follow, no longer like before when collective debate was confused and vast with no master.
translations.idiomatic: He urged clear trunk and branch policies so the nation would know the railway program and end chaotic debate.

sentences.zh: 當此時事日亟，邊防最要。

translations.literal: At this time affairs daily grow urgent; frontier defense is most important.
translations.idiomatic: With crises mounting, frontier defense was paramount.

sentences.zh: 國家若不趕將東西南北諸大幹路迅速次第興築，則強鄰四逼，無所措手。

translations.literal: If the state does not hurry to build the great trunk routes east, west, south, and north rapidly in sequence, then powerful neighbors press on four sides and there is no place to apply one's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Without rapid trunk lines in every direction, encirclement by strong neighbors would leave China helpless.

sentences.zh: 人民不足責，其如大局何。

translations.literal: The people are not enough to blame; what of the overall situation?
translations.idiomatic: The people could not be blamed; the strategic stakes could not.

sentences.zh: 此中利害，間不容髮。

translations.literal: The profit and harm herein allow no hair's breadth of delay.
translations.idiomatic: The stakes admitted no delay.

sentences.zh: 惟有仰懇乾綱獨斷，不再游移。

translations.literal: Only to look up and beg the imperial decision alone, no longer wavering.
translations.idiomatic: He begged the throne for decisive, unwavering action.

sentences.zh: 在德、奧、法、日本、墨西哥諸國，其鐵路均歸國有，而我分枝路與民，已為優異。

translations.literal: In Germany, Austria, France, Japan, Mexico, and other states their railways are all state-owned, while we give branch routes to the people—already a preferential exception.
translations.idiomatic: Germany, Austria, France, Japan, and Mexico nationalized railways; China already privileged merchants with branches.

sentences.zh: 況幹枝相輔，上下相維，於理尚順，於事稍易。

translations.literal: Moreover trunk and branch assist each other, upper and lower link—reasonable in principle and somewhat easier in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Trunks and branches mutually supported one another—sound in theory and easier in practice.

sentences.zh: 此路政之大綱，亟宜明定辦法者一也。

translations.literal: This great outline of road administration urgently needs a clear fixed method—first point.
translations.idiomatic: Clear railway policy was his first recommendation.

sentences.zh: 又東南幹路，以粵漢議辦為最早。

translations.literal: Also the southeastern trunk, with Guangdong–Hankou discussed earliest.
translations.idiomatic: The southeastern trunk, Guangdong–Hankou, had been debated earliest.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，督辦大臣會同湖廣總督等奏准借美款興造。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu the superintendent minister together with the Huguang governor-general and others memorialized approval to borrow American funds for construction.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 officials approved an American loan to build it.

sentences.zh: 當時訂定合同後，業已築成粵省之佛山三水鐵路一百餘里，廣州至英德幹路亦已購地開工。

translations.literal: After the contract was fixed at the time, more than a hundred li of the Foshan–Sanshui railway in Guangdong province had already been built, and the Guangzhou–Yingde trunk had also purchased land and begun work.
translations.idiomatic: Under the contract, over a hundred li from Foshan to Sanshui were built and the Guangzhou–Yingde trunk had begun.

sentences.zh: 乃三十年春間，張之洞忽信王先謙等之言，不惜鉅資，經向美公司廢約，堅持固執，卒至停罷。

translations.literal: Yet in spring of the thirtieth year Zhang Zhidong suddenly believed the words of Wang Xianqian and others, not sparing huge funds, and after negotiating with the American company voided the contract, holding stubbornly until work stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Guangxu 30 spring Zhang Zhidong, heeding Wang Xianqian, spent heavily to cancel the American contract and halted work.

sentences.zh: 廢約後，原欲集鄂、湘、粵三省之力以成此路。

translations.literal: After voiding the contract, the original intent was to gather the strength of E, Xiang, and Yue provinces to complete this route.
translations.idiomatic: Cancellation was meant to let Hubei, Hunan, and Guangdong finish the line together.

sentences.zh: 詎悠忽數年，粵則有款而紳士爭權，辦路甚少，湘、鄂則集款無著，徒糜局費。

translations.literal: Alas, years passed idly; Yue had funds but gentry fought over power and built little road; Xiang and E gathered no funds and only wasted bureau expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed: Guangdong had money but factional strife; Hunan and Hubei raised little and wasted bureau funds.

sentences.zh: 張之洞翻然悔悟，不護前非，仍擬借款築造，乃向英、德、法三國銀行訂定借款草合同，籤押後正欲入告，因美國援案插入，暫緩陳奏。

translations.literal: Zhidong repented and changed, not protecting former errors, and still planned borrowing to build; he then signed draft loan contracts with English, German, and French banks, and after signing was about to report when the American case intervened and memorialization was temporarily delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang repented and drafted loans with British, German, and French banks, but an American diplomatic case delayed submission.

sentences.zh: 張之洞旋即病故，此事遂一擱至今。

translations.literal: Zhidong soon fell ill and died; the matter was set aside until today.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang died before completing the plan, and the project languished.

sentences.zh: 計自廢約以來，已閱七載。

translations.literal: Counting from voiding the contract, seven years have already passed.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years had passed since cancellation.

sentences.zh: 倘若無此翻覆，粵漢早已告成，亦如京漢，已屆十年還本之期矣。

translations.literal: If not for this reversal, Guangdong–Hankou would long ago have been completed, like Jing-Han already reaching the ten-year principal repayment period.
translations.idiomatic: Without the reversal, Guangdong–Hankou might have been finished like Jing-Han, already in its ten-year repayment period.

sentences.zh: 至川漢集款，皆屬取諸田間，其款確有一千餘萬。

translations.literal: As for Sichuan–Hankou fund-raising, all was taken from the fields; the funds truly exceeded ten million.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan–Hankou funds, drawn from the countryside, truly exceeded ten million.

sentences.zh: 紳士樹黨，各懷意見，上年始由宜昌開工至歸州以東，此五百里工程，尚不及十分之二三，不知何年方能告竣。

translations.literal: Gentry formed factions, each harboring opinions; only last year did work begin from Yichang east to east of Guizhou—this five-hundred-li project is still less than two or three tenths complete; one does not know what year it can be finished.
translations.idiomatic: Factional Sichuan gentry had begun only a fraction of the five hundred li east from Yichang toward Guizhou, with no end in sight.

sentences.zh: 而施典章擅將川路租股之所入，倒帳竟至數百萬之多。

translations.literal: Yet Shi Dianzhang arbitrarily used Sichuan railway rent-share receipts and defrauded accounts reaching several million.
translations.idiomatic: Official Shi Dianzhang had embezzled millions from Sichuan railway rent shares.

sentences.zh: 此又川、粵、漢幹路之潰敗延誤，亟宜查辦者又一也。

translations.literal: This again is the collapse and delay of the Chuan, Yue, and Han trunk routes—urgently needing investigation—another point.
translations.idiomatic: The failure of the Sichuan, Guangdong, and Hankou trunks required investigation—his second point.

sentences.zh: 近來雲貴督臣李經羲議造滇桂邊路，於國防尤有關係。

translations.literal: Recently Yunnan–Guizhou Governor Li Jingxi debated building the Yunnan–Guizhou frontier route, especially related to national defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan–Guizhou Governor Li Jingxi's proposed frontier line mattered greatly for defense.

sentences.zh: 然不有粵漢幹路自湖南之永興與廣西之全州相接，則滇桂路何能自守？

translations.literal: Yet without the Guangdong–Hankou trunk connecting Yongxing in Hunan with Quanzhou in Guangxi, how could the Yunnan–Guizhou route defend itself?
translations.idiomatic: But without Guangdong–Hankou linking Hunan's Yongxing to Guangxi's Quanzhou, the frontier line could not stand alone.

sentences.zh: 今我粵漢直貫桂滇，川漢遠控西藏，實為國家應有兩大幹路，萬一有事，緩急可恃。

translations.literal: Now our Guangdong–Hankou runs straight through Gui and Dian, and Sichuan–Hankou controls Tibet from afar—they are truly the two great trunk routes the state should have; if anything occurs, in urgency or leisure they can be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong–Hankou through Guangxi and Yunnan and Sichuan–Hankou toward Tibet were the two strategic trunks the state needed.

sentences.zh: 故無論袤延數千里之幹路，斷非民間零星湊集之款所能圖成，即使遲以十年或二十年，造成之後，而各分畛域，倘於有事之際，命令不行，仍必如東西洋之議歸國家收買。

translations.literal: Therefore no matter trunk routes extending several thousand li, they cannot be accomplished by scattered popular funds pieced together; even if delayed ten or twenty years until built, yet each guards its own domain—if in time of trouble orders are not obeyed, it will still be like East and West foreign countries' debate to return to state purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-li trunks could not rely on scattered private funds; even if built slowly, divided control in crisis would force nationalization as in the West.

sentences.zh: 此幹路之必歸國有者又一也。

translations.literal: That trunk routes must return to state ownership is another point.
translations.idiomatic: Trunk lines must therefore be state-owned—his third point.

sentences.zh: 國家成法，待民寬厚，雖當財賦極困難之時，不肯加賦。

translations.literal: State established law treats the people generously; even when state revenue is extremely difficult, it is unwilling to add levies.
translations.idiomatic: State law treated the people generously and avoided new taxes even in fiscal crisis.

sentences.zh: 四川、湖南現因興造鐵路，創為租股名目，每畝帶徵，以充路款。

translations.literal: Sichuan and Hunan now, because of building railways, created the name of rent shares, with additional collection per mu to supply road funds.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan and Hunan now levied per-mu railway rent shares for construction funds.

sentences.zh: 聞兩省農民，正深訾怨，偶遇荒年，追呼尤覺難堪。

translations.literal: It is heard that farmers in the two provinces deeply resent this; when famine years come, collection is especially hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers in both provinces deeply resented the surcharges, especially in famine years when collection became unbearable.

sentences.zh: 但路局以路亡地亡之說驚哧愚民，遂不得不從。

translations.literal: But the road bureau used the saying that if the road is lost the land is lost to frighten and coerce the foolish people, and they had no choice but to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Road bureaus terrified peasants with warnings that losing the railway meant losing the land, leaving no choice but compliance.

sentences.zh: 川省民力較紓，尚能勉強擔負。

translations.literal: Sichuan's popular strength was relatively easier; they could still barely bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan could still barely bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 湘民本非饒足，若數年之間，強逼百姓出此數千鉅萬之重貲，而路工一日不完，路利一日無著，深恐民窮財盡，欲圖富強而轉滋貧弱。

translations.literal: Hunan people were originally not affluent; if within several years the common people were forced to produce these tens of millions in heavy funds, while road work was not finished in a day and road profit had no return in a day, I deeply fear the people would be impoverished and funds exhausted, seeking to become rich and strong yet instead growing poorer and weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was poorer: forcing millions in payments while lines stayed unfinished would impoverish the people instead of strengthening the state.

sentences.zh: 是以幹路收歸國有，命下之日，薄海百姓，必無阻撓之慮。

translations.literal: Therefore when trunk routes return to state ownership, from the day the order descends, all within the four seas will surely have no worry of obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Nationalizing trunks would end popular resistance.

sentences.zh: 況留此民力以造枝路，其工易成，其資易集，其利易收。

translations.literal: Moreover, reserving this popular strength to build branch routes—the work is easy to complete, funds easy to gather, profits easy to collect.
translations.idiomatic: Freed capital could build branches more easily, cheaply, and profitably.

sentences.zh: 使其土貨得以暢行，民間漸資饒富，此枝路之可歸民有者又一也。

translations.literal: Letting local goods circulate freely, the people gradually grow affluent—this is another reason branch routes may belong to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Branches could let local goods flow and enrich the people—his second reason for private branch lines.

sentences.zh: 疏上，下所司議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, it was sent down to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「中國幅員遼闊，邊疆袤延數萬里，程途動需數閱月之久，朝廷每念邊防，輒勞宵旰。

translations.literal: An edict said: "China's territory is vast and broad; the frontier extends tens of thousands of li; journeys often require several months. The court whenever it thinks of frontier defense is troubled day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The throne declared that China's vast frontiers required months to cross and kept rulers sleepless over defense.

sentences.zh: 欲資控御，惟有速造鐵路之一策。

translations.literal: To supply control, there is only the one policy of rapidly building railways.
translations.idiomatic: Only rapid railway construction could secure control.

sentences.zh: 況憲政之諮謀，軍務之徵調，土產之運輸，胥賴交通便利，大局始有轉機。

translations.literal: Moreover constitutional deliberation, military levy and transfer, and transport of native products all rely on convenient communications before the overall situation can turn.
translations.idiomatic: Constitutional government, military mobilization, and commerce all needed transport to improve.

sentences.zh: 熟籌再四，國家必有縱橫四境諸大幹路，方足以資行政而握中央之樞紐。

translations.literal: After mature deliberation again and again, the state must have great trunk routes running vertically and horizontally through the four borders before it suffices to administer and grasp the pivot of the center.
translations.idiomatic: The state needed trunk lines in every direction to govern and hold the center.

sentences.zh: 從前規畫未善，並無一定辦法，以致全國鐵路，錯亂紛歧，不分枝幹，不量民力，一紙呈請，輒行批准商辦。

translations.literal: Former planning was not sound and there was no fixed method, causing the whole country's railways to be confused and divergent, not distinguishing branch and trunk, not measuring popular strength—a single sheet memorialized and merchant operation was promptly approved.
translations.idiomatic: Past policy had approved merchant lines without distinguishing trunk from branch or measuring popular capacity, producing chaos.

sentences.zh: 乃數年以來，粵則收股及半，造路無多；

translations.literal: Yet for several years Yue collected only half its shares and built little road;
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong raised only half its shares and built little;

sentences.zh: 川則倒帳甚鉅，參追無著；

translations.literal: Chuan had huge defalcations with no recovery in investigation;
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan suffered massive embezzlement without recovery;

sentences.zh: 湘、鄂則開局多年，徒資坐耗。

translations.literal: Xiang and E opened bureaus for many years, only consuming funds in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Hubei bureaus consumed funds for years without progress.

sentences.zh: 竭萬民之脂膏，或以虛糜，或以侵蝕，恐曠時愈久，民累愈深，上下交受其害，貽誤何堪設想。

translations.literal: Exhausting the fat and cream of ten thousand people, either wasted in vain or eroded— I fear the longer time passes the deeper the people's burden, upper and lower jointly suffering harm—how can one bear to imagine the delay.
translations.idiomatic: Popular wealth was wasted or stolen; delay would deepen misery for court and people alike.

sentences.zh: 用特明白曉諭，昭示天下，幹路均歸國有，定為政策。

translations.literal: Therefore I specially make clear proclamation to all under Heaven: trunk routes all return to state ownership, fixed as policy.
translations.idiomatic: The throne proclaimed nationalization of trunk lines as fixed policy.

sentences.zh: 所有宣統三年以前，各省分設公司、集股商辦之幹路，延誤已久，應即由國家收回，趕緊興築。

translations.literal: All trunk routes in the various provinces set up as companies and merchant-built with shares before the third year of Xuantong, long delayed, should immediately be recovered by the state and hurriedly built.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant trunk projects approved before Xuantong 3 would be nationalized and rushed to completion.

sentences.zh: 除枝路仍准商民量力酌行外，其從前批准幹路各案，一律取消。

translations.literal: Except branch routes still permitted to merchants and people according to capacity, all formerly approved trunk cases are uniformly canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Branches might still be built privately; prior trunk approvals were voided.

sentences.zh: 至應如何收回之詳細辦法，著度支部、郵傳部悉心籌畫，迅速請旨辦理。

translations.literal: As for detailed methods of how to recover them, the Ministry of Revenue and the Ministry of Posts and Communications are to plan carefully and quickly request imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministries of Revenue and Communications were to plan recovery details.

sentences.zh: 度支部奏：「粵、川、湘、鄂四省所抽所招之公司股票，盡數收回，由度支、郵傳兩部特出國家鐵路股票，常年六釐給息。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "Shares levied and subscribed in Guangdong, Sichuan, Hunan, and Hubei provinces are all to be bought back; the Ministries of Revenue and Posts will specially issue state railway shares paying six percent interest annually.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue proposed buying back four-province shares with new state railway bonds at six percent annual interest.

sentences.zh: 嗣後如有餘利，按股分給。

translations.literal: If hereafter there is surplus profit, distribution follows shares.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus profits would be divided among shareholders.

sentences.zh: 倘原抽本，五年後亦可分十五年抽本。

translations.literal: If the original principal is desired, after five years principal may be drawn over fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Original principal could be withdrawn over fifteen years beginning after five years.

sentences.zh: 其不原換國家鐵路股票者，均准分別辦理，以昭平允。

translations.literal: Those not wishing to exchange for state railway shares may all be handled separately to show fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Those refusing state bonds would receive separate fair terms.

sentences.zh: 粵路全系商股，因路工停頓，糜費太甚，票價不及五成。

translations.literal: The Guangdong route is entirely merchant shares; because road work stopped, waste was too great, and share prices did not reach half.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong shares, with construction stalled, traded below half face value.

sentences.zh: 現每股從優發給六成，其虧耗之四成，發給國家無利股票。

translations.literal: Now each share is preferentially paid sixty percent; the forty percent loss is issued in state non-interest-bearing shares.
translations.idiomatic: Holders would receive sixty percent cash and forty percent in non-interest state stock.

sentences.zh: 路成獲利之日，准在本路餘利項下，分十年攤給。

translations.literal: When the road is completed and profit obtained, amortization over ten years from this route's surplus profit is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The forty percent loss could be repaid from profits over ten years after completion.

sentences.zh: 湘路商本，照本發還。

translations.literal: Hunan merchant capital is repaid at principal.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan merchant principal would be repaid in full.

sentences.zh: 其米捐、租股等款，准發給國家保利股本。

translations.literal: Rice levies, rent shares, and other funds may be issued state principal-guaranteed interest-bearing capital shares.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan rice levies and rent shares would become state guaranteed bonds.

sentences.zh: 鄂路商股，並准一律照本發還。

translations.literal: Hubei merchant shares are also all permitted repayment at principal.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei merchant shares would likewise be repaid at principal.

sentences.zh: 其因路動用賑糶捐款，准照湖南米捐辦理。

translations.literal: Funds from relief grain donations used for the road may be handled like Hunan rice levies.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei relief grain funds used for the railway would follow Hunan rice-levy terms.

sentences.zh: 川路宜昌實用工料之款四百數十萬兩，准給國家保利股票。

translations.literal: Sichuan road funds actually used for engineering at Yichang, four million-odd taels, may be issued state principal-guaranteed shares.
translations.idiomatic: Four million taels spent at Yichang would become state guaranteed bonds.

sentences.zh: 其現存七百餘萬兩，原否入股，或歸本省興辦實業，仍聽其便。

translations.literal: The existing seven million-odd taels—whether to invest in shares or devote to provincial industry in the province—is still left to their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Seven million taels still on hand could be invested or used for provincial industry as locals chose.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 詔停川、湘兩省租股。

translations.literal: An edict halted rent shares in Sichuan and Hunan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan and Hunan rent-share levies were stopped.

sentences.zh: 起端方以侍郎督辦粵漢、川漢鐵路。

translations.literal: Duanfang was raised from vice minister to supervise Guangdong–Hankou and Sichuan–Hankou railways.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Duanfang was appointed to supervise Guangdong–Hankou and Sichuan–Hankou.

sentences.zh: 其粵漢、川漢，英、德、法三國借款，亦即簽訂。

translations.literal: For Guangdong–Hankou and Sichuan–Hankou, English, German, and French loans were also signed.
translations.idiomatic: Anglo-German-French loans for those lines were signed.

sentences.zh: 方幹路收歸國有之詔既頒，湘、粵人士群起譁譟，力謀抗拒，顧未久即定。

translations.literal: When the edict on trunk nationalization was promulgated, Hunan and Guangdong people rose in uproar and strove to resist, yet before long it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Nationalization sparked uproar in Hunan and Guangdong but subsided quickly.

sentences.zh: 護川督王人文代陳川諮議局請緩接收川路，詔旨斥之。

translations.literal: Acting Sichuan Governor Wang Renwen reported on behalf of the Sichuan consultative assembly requesting delayed takeover of the Sichuan road; an edict rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Governor Wang Renwen sought delay; the court rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 川人羅綸等言：「部臣對待川民，均以威力從事，毫不持平。

translations.literal: Sichuan men Luo Lun and others said: "Ministry officials treat Sichuan people with power in every matter, utterly without fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan delegates led by Luo Lun accused the ministry of coercion without fairness.

sentences.zh: 」人文復據以上聞，仍嚴斥之。

translations.literal: " Wang Renwen again reported upward; they were again sternly rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Wang reported again and was rebuked again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以趙爾豐署四川總督。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao Erfeng was appointed acting Sichuan governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Erfeng became acting governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 川人因路事持久不決，始以罷市、罷課，抗糧、抗捐，發布自保商榷書；

translations.literal: Because the road affair long remained unresolved, Sichuan people first boycotted markets and classes, resisted grain taxes and levies, and issued a self-protection discussion book;
translations.idiomatic: Unresolved railway disputes led to market and school boycotts, tax resistance, and self-protection manifestos;

sentences.zh: 繼則集眾圍攻督署，再攻省垣。

translations.literal: then they gathered crowds to besiege the governor's yamen, then attacked the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: then sieges of the governor's yamen and provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 遂命端方率軍入川。

translations.literal: Duanfang was then ordered to lead troops into Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Duanfang was sent with troops into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 又以川事日棘，命前粵督岑春煊赴川辦理剿撫。

translations.literal: Because Sichuan affairs grew daily more acute, former Guangdong Governor Cen Chunxuan was ordered to Sichuan to handle suppression and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Chunxuan was ordered to Sichuan to pacify the crisis.

sentences.zh: 春煊既受命，請以現金償川省路股，桂撫沈秉堃亦以為言，部議借英金三百萬鎊，不能決也。

translations.literal: Once Cen received the order, he requested repaying Sichuan road shares in cash; Guangxi Governor Shen Bingheng also spoke thus; ministry deliberation borrowed £3,000,000 sterling but could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Cen sought cash repayment for Sichuan shares; the ministry debated a £3 million loan without resolution.

sentences.zh: 春煊至鄂，會成都圍解，稱疾不往。

translations.literal: Cen reached E; when the Chengdu siege was lifted he claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Cen reached Hubei, then pleaded illness after Chengdu was relieved and never entered Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 御史陳善同上章，請罷斥郵傳大臣盛宣懷，以弭巨變。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Shantong memorialized requesting dismissal of Posts and Communications Minister Sheng Xuanhuai to quell great upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Shantong demanded Sheng Xuanhuai's dismissal to avert catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「竊維國以民為本，自古未有得民心而國不興者，即未有失民心而不危者。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "I respectfully consider that the state takes the people as foundation; from antiquity there has never been gaining the people's hearts while the state did not rise, nor losing the people's hearts without danger.
translations.idiomatic: Chen wrote that states rise and fall with popular support.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『眾怒難犯。

translations.literal: The Classic of Changes says: 'The multitude's wrath is hard to offend.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: 'Mass anger is dangerous to provoke.'

sentences.zh: 』書曰：『民可近，不可下。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: 'The people may be approached, not looked down upon.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: 'The people must be approached, not despised.'

sentences.zh: 』此中消息至微。

translations.literal: The message herein is extremely subtle.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson was subtle but grave.

sentences.zh: 此次以鐵路幹線歸國有，政策本極相宜。

translations.literal: This time making railway trunk lines state-owned—the policy itself is extremely suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Nationalizing trunks was sound policy in itself.

sentences.zh: 比者屢詔蠲除各項雜捐，所以恤民者，固已仁至義盡。

translations.literal: Recently repeated edicts remitted various miscellaneous levies—the means of comforting the people have already been benevolent to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Recent tax remissions had already shown imperial benevolence.

sentences.zh: 而湘、粵等省人心惶駭，擾擾不靖，川患且日以加劇者，則以郵傳大臣盛宣懷於此事之辦理實有未善也。

translations.literal: Yet Hunan, Guangdong, and other provinces' hearts are fearful and disturbed, and Sichuan's trouble grows daily worse, because Posts and Communications Minister Sheng Xuanhuai in handling this matter truly had shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hunan, Guangdong, and especially Sichuan grew turbulent because Sheng Xuanhuai handled the transition badly.

sentences.zh: 各路商辦之局，其始皆歷奉先皇帝諭旨，根據大清商律。

translations.literal: The various merchant-operated bureaus at the start all successively received former emperor's edicts based on the Great Qing commercial code.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant railway companies had operated under imperial sanction and commercial law.

sentences.zh: 如欲改歸官辦，自應統籌全局，劃定年限，分期分段，量力遞收，於國於民，方為兩利。

translations.literal: If one wishes to change to government operation, one should plan the overall situation, fix years, divide periods and sections, and recover according to capacity in stages—for state and people both benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Nationalization should have been gradual, staged, and fair to state and people alike.

sentences.zh: 今盛宣懷事前毫無預備，徒仰仗借款，突然將批准各案奏請一律取消。

translations.literal: Now Sheng Xuanhuai made no preparation beforehand, relying only on borrowing, and suddenly memorialized canceling all approved cases uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had prepared nothing, relied on foreign loans, and abruptly canceled all approvals.

sentences.zh: 各路以十餘年之經營，千數百萬之籌集，一旦盡取諸其懷而奪之。

translations.literal: Each route, with more than ten years of management and tens of millions raised, was in one morning taken from their bosoms and seized.
translations.idiomatic: Decades of investment and hundreds of millions were seized overnight.

sentences.zh: 而所訂借款合同，利率之高，虛折之多，抵押之鉅，債權之重，又著著失敗，予人口實。

translations.literal: Yet the loan contracts signed—high interest, heavy discount, huge collateral, heavy creditor rights—again plainly failed and gave others handle.
translations.idiomatic: Loan terms were ruinous: high interest, heavy discounts, vast collateral, and crushing creditor power.

sentences.zh: 各省人民，痛念前勞，怵心後禍，宜其奔走駭告，岌岌若不終日也。

translations.literal: People of the various provinces, pained at former labor and alarmed at later calamity, rightly ran about in terror as if each day were not the last.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces mourned past sacrifices and feared future loss, spreading panic.

sentences.zh: 查給事中石長信之請定幹路、枝路辦法，在四月初七日；

translations.literal: Investigation shows Giving-Remonstrance Shi Changxin's request to fix trunk and branch methods on the seventh day of the fourth month;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Changxin had proposed trunk-branch policy on the fourth month's seventh day;

sentences.zh: 郵傳部之覆奏，宣布國有政策，在十一日；

translations.literal: the Ministry of Posts and Communications' reply memorial announcing state ownership policy on the eleventh;
translations.idiomatic: the ministry announced nationalization on the eleventh;

sentences.zh: 而借款合同之籤押，在二十二日。

translations.literal: yet the loan contract was signed on the twenty-second.
translations.idiomatic: loan contracts were signed on the twenty-second.

sentences.zh: 似政策之改定，實緣借款而發生也者。

translations.literal: It seems the policy change was in fact born from borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: Nationalization appeared driven by borrowing, not planning.

sentences.zh: 舉辦此等大事，乃平時漫無布置，出以猝遽如此，反使朝廷減輕民累之恉晦沒不彰。

translations.literal: Undertaking such great affairs with no layout in normal times and acting so hastily instead made the court's intent to lighten popular burdens obscure.
translations.idiomatic: Haste and lack of planning obscured the court's intent to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 而復不能審慎臨機，強令宜歸工程每月工項仍由川款開支，實與五月二十一日上諭『川路仍存七百餘萬，原否入股，或辦實業，並聽其便』等語大相違背。

translations.literal: Yet unable to judge the moment carefully, forcibly ordering that monthly engineering expenses still be paid from Sichuan funds truly greatly contradicted the edict of the twenty-first day of the fifth month that 'the seven million-odd taels of Sichuan road still stored, whether to invest in shares or run industry, is left to their convenience.'
translations.idiomatic: Forcing Sichuan funds to pay monthly engineering costs violated the May 21 edict leaving seven million taels to local choice.

sentences.zh: 必欲使我皇上體恤商民之恩，壅遏之不使下逮，陷朝廷以不信，示天下以可疑，群起抵抗，何怪其然。

translations.literal: They must make our emperor's grace in cherishing merchants blocked from reaching below, trap the court in distrust, show all under Heaven suspicion—mass resistance, how can one blame them?
translations.idiomatic: Blocking imperial mercy, breaking trust, and inviting suspicion made resistance inevitable.

sentences.zh: 幸以國家三百年來深仁厚澤，淪浹人心，故雖眾怨交集於盛宣懷，終無敢有歸怨朝廷者。

translations.literal: Fortunately through the state's three hundred years of deep benevolence saturating hearts, though all resentment converged on Sheng Xuanhuai, none dared blame the court.
translations.idiomatic: Three centuries of Qing benevolence kept blame on Sheng, not the throne.

sentences.zh: 比聞川省風潮日烈，皆以盛宣懷喪權誤國，欲得而甘心。

translations.literal: Recently heard Sichuan's unrest grows daily fierce; all say Sheng Xuanhuai lost rights and harmed the state and wish to have his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan unrest intensified; crowds blamed Sheng for betraying national rights.

sentences.zh: 月餘以來，屢開全省股東大會，每次到者近萬人，誓與路為存亡，在場之人無不為之泣下。

translations.literal: For more than a month provincial shareholder meetings were repeatedly held; each time nearly ten thousand attended, vowing life or death with the road—those present were all moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Shareholder meetings drew ten thousand who swore to live or die for the railway and wept.

sentences.zh: 合十餘州縣地方，並相約不納錢糧，不上捐輸，學堂停課，商民罷市。

translations.literal: More than ten prefectures and counties likewise agreed not to pay taxes or levies, schools stopped classes, merchants closed markets.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen prefectures refused taxes and levies, closed schools, and shut markets.

sentences.zh: 各戶恭設先皇帝靈位，朝夕痛哭，人無樂生之心，士懷必死之志，愁慘蕭條，如經大劫，至可憐念。

translations.literal: Each household reverently set the late emperor's spirit tablet, weeping morning and evening; people had no heart for life, scholars harbored death-certain resolve—desolation like after great catastrophe, pitiable indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Households mourned the late emperor daily; despair spread like after a catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 夫今日皇皇失所之窮民，皆國家{袁皿}々在疚之赤子，情形狼狽至此，我皇上聞之，必有惻然動念者。

translations.literal: Today's destitute people wandering homeless are all the state's children whom the state anxiously cares for; their plight reached this point—our emperor hearing it must surely be moved with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Today's desperate poor were the children the state was bound to cherish; the emperor must pity their plight.

sentences.zh: 若不亟為拯救，萬一相持不解，稍延時日，或有不軌之徒，從中鼓煽，強者並命於尋仇，弱者絕望於逃死，眾志一睽，全體瓦解，終非國家福也。

translations.literal: If not quickly rescued, should stalemate continue and days extend, perhaps unscrupulous men will drum up trouble from within—the strong uniting lives in revenge, the weak despairing in flight—when wills diverge the whole body dissolves; in the end it is not the state's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Without swift rescue, stalemate could let agitators turn protest into revolt and dissolve the realm.

sentences.zh: 現在湘、鄂爭路，餘波尚未大熄，而雨水為災，幾近十省，盜匪成群，流亡遍野。

translations.literal: Now Hunan and Hubei railway struggles' afterwaves have not fully subsided, while rain disasters afflict nearly ten provinces, bandits gather in groups, and exiles cover the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Hubei unrest continued amid floods in ten provinces, banditry, and refugees.

sentences.zh: 若川省小有風鶴之警，恐由滇、藏以至沿江、沿海，必有起而應之者，其為患又豈止於路不能收而已。

translations.literal: If Sichuan has slight alarm like wind and crane, I fear from Yunnan and Tibet to the river and coast there will be those who rise in response—the harm is not only that roads cannot be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan unrest could spread from Yunnan and Tibet to the coast, far beyond railway policy.

sentences.zh: 頃者我皇上諭派鄂、粵、川、湘等省督撫，令於所轄境內鐵路事宜各得會同辦理。

translations.literal: Recently our emperor ordered governors of E, Yue, Chuan, Xiang and other provinces to jointly handle railway affairs within their jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: The throne had ordered multi-province cooperation on railway affairs.

sentences.zh: 盛宣懷剛愎自用，不洽輿情，已可概見，應如何懲處，以儆將來。

translations.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai is obstinate and self-willed, out of tune with public sentiment—this can be seen in outline; how he should be punished to warn the future.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's obstinacy and popular hatred demanded punishment as a warning.

sentences.zh: 至川民爭議，久懸不斷，終慮釀成鉅變。

translations.literal: As for Sichuan popular contention long suspended unresolved, in the end I fear it will brew great change.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's unresolved railway fight threatened greater upheaval.

sentences.zh: 應責成督辦、會辦各大臣，酌度情形，妥速維持，以息眾喙。

translations.literal: The supervising and co-supervising great ministers should be charged to gauge conditions and maintain order properly and swiftly to quiet the clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising ministers must restore order quickly.

sentences.zh: 」時宣懷入為郵傳大臣，幹路收歸國有、及息借外債築路、處分四省路股，實主其事，故善同及之，語至切直。

translations.literal: " At that time Xuanhuai had entered as Posts and Communications Minister; trunk nationalization, resting on foreign debt to build roads, and disposing of the four provinces' road shares—he really presided over these affairs, so Shantong implicated him, his language extremely forthright.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, as minister, had driven nationalization, foreign loans, and share seizure—Chen's memorial named him directly.

sentences.zh: 疏入不省。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 而川省溫江等十餘州縣民團，每起數千或萬人，所至焚掠，勢極猖獗。

translations.literal: Yet Sichuan's Wenjiang and more than ten prefectures' militia groups, each time several thousand or ten thousand, wherever they went burned and plundered—momentum extremely fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan militias of thousands burned and looted across Wenjiang and a dozen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大軍擊退之，旋據崇慶、新津、彭山，而嘉定、灌縣相繼失陷。

translations.literal: Great armies repelled them, then occupied Chongqing, Xinjin, and Pengshan, while Jiading and Guanxian fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops retook some towns while Jiading and Guanxian fell.

sentences.zh: 邛州軍隊譁變，汶川縣署被毀，命湘、鄂、陝諸軍赴援。

translations.literal: Qiongzhou troops mutinied, Wenchuan county yamen was destroyed; Hunan, Hubei, and Shaanxi armies were ordered to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Mutiny at Qiongzhou and destruction in Wenchuan brought reinforcements from Hunan, Hubei, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 會鄂事起，川亂愈亟，以岑春煊為川督，而川省旋為民軍所據，端方、趙爾豐均及於難。

translations.literal: When Hubei trouble arose, Sichuan disorder grew more urgent; Cen Chunxuan was made Sichuan governor, yet Sichuan was soon held by revolutionary troops; Duanfang and Zhao Erfeng both met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuchang uprising worsened Sichuan; though Cen was appointed governor, revolutionaries seized the province and Duanfang and Zhao Erfeng perished.

sentences.zh: 乃罷盛宣懷以謝川人，而國事已不可為矣。

translations.literal: Then Sheng Xuanhuai was dismissed to appease Sichuan people, yet national affairs were already beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was dismissed to appease Sichuan, but the dynasty was already doomed.

sentences.zh: 蓋論辦路之優劣，官辦則籌款易、竣工速，自非商辦可及。

translations.literal: Generally speaking of the merits and defects of building roads: government operation makes fund-raising easy and completion swift, naturally not what merchant operation can match.
translations.idiomatic: Official railways raised funds and finished faster than merchant lines.

sentences.zh: 而外債之虧耗，大權之旁落，弊害孔多，亦遠過於商路。

translations.literal: Yet losses on foreign debt, power falling aside, and harms numerous, also far surpass merchant roads.
translations.idiomatic: But foreign loans cost more and surrendered more control than merchant projects.

sentences.zh: 惟京張鐵路，以京奉餘利舉辦，詹天佑躬親其役，絲毫不假外人，允為中國自辦之路。

translations.literal: Only the Jing-Zhang railway, funded from Jing-Feng surplus profit, with Zhan Tianyou personally undertaking the work, not relying on foreigners in the slightest, may be called China's self-built road.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jing-Zhang, funded from Jing-Feng profits under Zhan Tianyou without foreign help, was truly Chinese-built.

sentences.zh: 而鄂之鐵廠，制鋼軌以應全國造路之需，挽回大利，尤為不鮮。

translations.literal: And Hubei's iron works, manufacturing steel rails to meet the whole nation's road-building needs and recover great profit, is especially not slight.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei's steel works supplying rails nationwide recovered major benefits.

sentences.zh: 統計官辦之路：*京漢長二千六百三十里，資本金一萬萬零五百六十二萬八千餘元。

translations.literal: Counting government-operated roads: * Jing-Han length 2,630 li, capital 105,628,000-odd yuan.
translations.idiomatic: * Jing-Han: 2,630 li, capital 105,628,000+ yuan.

sentences.zh: *京奉長二千二百四十六里，資本金五千零八十八萬四千餘元。

translations.literal: * Jing-Feng length 2,246 li, capital 50,884,000-odd yuan.
translations.idiomatic: * Jing-Feng: 2,246 li, capital 50,884,000+ yuan.

translations.literal: * Jin-Pu length 1,863 li, capital 80,490,000-odd yuan.
translations.idiomatic: * Jin-Pu: 1,863 li, capital 80,490,000+ yuan.

translations.idiomatic: * Jing-Zhang: 546 li, capital 10,320,000+ yuan.

translations.idiomatic: * Hu-Ning: 725 li, capital 36,530,000+ yuan.

translations.idiomatic: * Zheng-Tai: 623 li, capital 23,126,000+ yuan.

translations.literal: * Bian-Luo length 402 li, capital 20,500,000 yuan.
translations.idiomatic: * Bian-Luo: 402 li, capital 20,500,000 yuan.

translations.literal: * Dao-Qing length 330 li, capital 9,549,000-odd yuan.
translations.idiomatic: * Dao-Qing: 330 li, capital 9,549,000+ yuan.

sentences.zh: *廣九長三百零三里，資本金一千一百六十六萬二千餘元。

translations.literal: * Guang-Jiu length 303 li, capital 11,662,000-odd yuan.
translations.idiomatic: * Guang-Jiu: 303 li, capital 11,662,000+ yuan.
